The event is a horror-war story, and its architect's identity is one of its central reveals — go in knowing only that the vampires have never, ever been this organized, and ask yourself why now.

primers.name: Doom Ascendant — One World Under Doom — CONCEPT
primers.text: By 2025, Victor von Doom has accumulated the one thing he always lacked: the Sorcerer Supreme's mantle (taken in *Blood Hunt*'s fallout), added to his armor, his nation, and his will. Then he does the most Doom thing imaginable — he doesn't invade the world. He *saves* it, publicly, repeatedly, undeniably: ending wars, fixing crises, offering every nation prosperity under Latverian administration, until the world's governments ask him to rule. *One World Under Doom* asks the question Doom has posed since 1961 with the volume turned up: if the tyrant is genuinely better at this than the heroes and democracies — what exactly is the argument against him? Reed Richards has to find one. It's the best Doom story in decades, and it only works because you met him in primer 18.

primers.name: The Shi'ar Empire & Imperial — CONCEPT
primers.text: The Shi'ar are the oldest and most militarized of the great space empires: an avian-descended civilization ruled from the throneworld Chandilar, enforcers of galactic order through the Imperial Guard — a legion of super-powered champions led by Gladiator, a mohawked titan whose strength literally scales with his confidence. *Imperial*, Hickman's return to the cosmic board, is a story of thrones: assassinations, succession crises, and the great powers (Shi'ar, Kree-Skrull alliance, Wakanda's intergalactic empire, Nova's reborn corps) recalculating what the galaxy is after Krakoa and Judgment Day rearranged the pieces. If the Annihilation saga (primers 37–41) was cosmic war, *Imperial* is cosmic *statecraft* — same players, colder weapons.

primers.name: Doug Ramsey — Revelation
primers.text: Long-time readers know Doug Ramsey as Cypher: the New Mutants' gentle linguist, a mutant whose power is understanding any language, once the X-Men's most famously "useless" member in a fight and one of its most beloved souls. In the post-Krakoa era Doug has become something else — the Heir of Apocalypse, chosen in the *Heir of Apocalypse* succession contest, carrying a portion of En Sabah Nur's power and his doctrine's terrible logic. *Age of Revelation* shows a possible future built in his image: a mutant utopia spreading across America, enforced absolutely. The horror of it is that the architect is Doug — the kindest mutant — reasoning his way, step by defensible step, to Apocalypse's conclusions. Watch the reasoning, not just the result.

primers.name: The New Ultimate Universe — Earth-6160 — SIDE TRACK S
primers.text: The essential side track of the modern era, anchored where it launches: the Maker (primer 60) escaped the end of his own universe and found a new one — a world he could reach *before* its heroes happened, and quietly edit: stealing destinies, delaying origins, ruling from behind a council of proxies for decades. Earth-6160 is that world: a Marvel Universe with its history stolen, where a middle-aged Peter Parker only now receives his powers, where the Ultimates are a resistance network with a countdown clock, and where every title is racing the Maker's return. It is deliberately readable as its own complete saga alongside the main order — and the guide's suggested windows (notably: binge it after Blood Hunt) are in Era 06 Part S. When the Maker's countdown ends, it ends for both tracks.

primers.name: The Maker's Council & The Children of Tomorrow — 6160 CONCEPT
primers.text: How do you rule a world whose heroes you prevented? The Maker governs Earth-6160 through a shadow council of regional powers — among them a Hulk who rules through weaponized serenity, a Captain America who never was, and Emmanuel da Costa's solar empire — each granted a territory in exchange for keeping history on rails. His original instrument, the Children of Tomorrow, were his accelerated-evolution army from the City: post-human, beautiful, and expendable. The 6160 track's tension is structural: a world designed by a villain, populated by people who don't know their lives were edited. Every hero who emerges there is a glitch in the Maker's design — which is why he counts glitches so carefully. ---

primers.name: The Stepford Cuckoos
primers.text: Five identical blonde telepaths — Celeste, Esme, Irma, Phoebe, and Sophie — who arrive at Xavier's school as Emma Frost's prize students and operate as a single hive mind: five bodies, one cold, precise, faintly contemptuous personality, finishing each other's sentences in chorus. Where Emma performs warmth as strategy, her Cuckoos don't bother performing at all. They are the student body's aristocracy and its early-warning system, loyal to Emma and to each other before any cause. A hive mind is a formidable thing — until one of the five starts thinking something the others don't share.

primers.name: Laura Kinney — X-23
primers.text: A teenage girl found among New York's homeless mutant runaways: two claws in each hand, one in each foot, a healing factor that never switches off — Wolverine's exact signature in a kid who barely speaks. *NYX* tells you almost nothing about where she came from, and the silence is the point: Laura Kinney — "X-23" in files she has never seen — is a person whose past was done *to* her, by people who built her as a weapon. The guide excavates how she was made later, in her own books. Start here, with what it costs a weapon to try being a person.

primers.name: The Red Skull — Johann Schmidt
primers.text: A hotel bellboy Hitler personally molded into the Nazi ideal: Captain America's oldest enemy, his face the ideology made literal. The Skull has died before; it didn't take. As Brubaker's run opens he is back in play — his consciousness lodged inside the mind of Russian oligarch Aleksander Lukin, two monsters sharing one body and one long patience. The Skull doesn't want to beat Steve Rogers in a fight. He wants to rot everything Steve stands for, slowly, from inside the century that replaced the war. Every Captain America story in this era is partly his.

primers.name: Daken
primers.text: Wolverine has a son. Logan never knew: the boy was cut from his murdered mother's womb in 1946, raised in secrecy, and taught one lesson above all others — his absent father is the reason for every bad thing in his life. Daken (the name is an insult in two languages) carries his father's claws and healing, plus a pheromone gift for bending a room's emotions, and none of Logan's hard-won restraint. *Origins* seeds him in shadow; the full reveal lands just past this era. When father and son finally meet, it will not be a reunion. Someone spent sixty years making sure of that.

primers.name: Maria Hill
primers.text: When Nick Fury vanishes, his chair doesn't go to a legend — it goes to Maria Hill, a career S.H.I.E.L.D. soldier with no mystique, no serum, and a by-the-book streak a mile wide. As *Civil War* opens she is the acting director enforcing registration, and she moves to arrest Captain America before the law she's enforcing has even passed. Hill is what the security state looks like without a spymaster's romance: competent, rigid, certain the file is right. Track her across the guide — her stands and her compromises map exactly how far the institution drifts in Fury's absence.

primers.name: Exodus
primers.text: Bennet du Paris was a twelfth-century crusader before Apocalypse remade him — an immensely powerful telekinetic who has spent eight centuries as a true believer, transferring his devotion from cause to cause without ever losing its intensity. In the Messiah era he leads the Acolytes, mutantkind's most zealous faithful, and he comes for the first mutant baby as a worshipper, not a strategist: Hope Summers is his religion made flesh. Exodus is the X-line's holy warrior — frightening not because he is cruel, but because he is sincere, and because a man who has buried eight centuries of certainties will always find a new one.

primers.name: Amadeus Cho
primers.text: A Korean-American teenager whose hypertrophied brain runs physics like a video game — trajectories, probabilities, outcomes, computed in real time — which, by his own cheerful ranking, makes him about the seventh smartest person on Earth. He enters the guide on the Hulk's side of World War Hulk, insisting the math proves Banner never kills the innocent, then stays on as Hercules' sidekick and conscience. Cho is the era's optimism engine: the kid who believes every monster in this guide is one correct calculation away from being saved. The guide will test that belief for twenty years.

primers.name: Abigail Brand
primers.text: Abigail Brand commands S.W.O.R.D., the orbital agency whose whole job is the day the aliens invade — which, in this era, is most days. Half-alien herself (she keeps the green hair; the rest she files down), Brand is the most pragmatic person in any room she enters: she frees Reed Richards mid-invasion, treats diplomacy as a targeting problem, and answers to results rather than to anyone's chain of command. The X-Men find her useful and unnerving in equal measure. Keep that ratio in mind. Brand recurs across the entire guide, and her loyalties are never as simple as her competence.

primers.name: The Hood — Parker Robbins
primers.text: Parker Robbins was a nobody — a small-time crook with a sick mother and a baby coming — until he shot a demon in an empty warehouse and took its cloak and boots. The cloak lets him walk on air and vanish; it also comes from somewhere infernal, and the price schedule is deliberately unclear. Robbins' real talent isn't power, it's organization: while the heroes tear themselves apart, he builds the underworld its first syndicate — supervillains with a union, a pension plan, and a boss. By Dark Reign he sits at Osborn's own table. The Hood is this era's proof that vacuums get filled from below.

primers.name: Legion — David Haller
primers.text: David Haller is Professor Xavier's son, and the strongest argument in the guide that power and damage scale together. David is an omega-level mutant whose fractured mind houses hundreds of distinct personalities — and each personality holds a different power, so whichever one is driving decides what David can do, and David is not always driving. He returns to the X-Men's world in the run-up to *Second Coming* as a catastrophe other people manage, not a person anyone thinks to ask. That is the tragedy the later books inherit: the most powerful mutant alive is a crowd, and the boy in the middle just wants a turn at his own life.

primers.name: Baron Zemo — Helmut Zemo
primers.anchor_series: Captain America — the Trial of Captain America setup
primers.text: Helmut Zemo, thirteenth Baron Zemo: son of the Nazi scientist whose death Captain America helped cause, his own face melted into his mask by his father's chemicals. Zemo has led the Masters of Evil and once ran the Thunderbolts as a long con in a hero's costume — his lifelong thesis being that the world is safer *ruled*, preferably by him. In this era his weapon of choice is information: he leaks the Winter Soldier's past to the world and lets courts and cameras accomplish what armies couldn't. Wherever Captain America's legacy is being contested, expect Zemo to already be there, smiling behind the mask.

primers.name: Sam Alexander — Nova
primers.text: You glimpsed him for one page in *Avengers vs. X-Men* — a helmeted kid crash-landing with the Nova Corps' last warning. His own series explains: Sam Alexander is fifteen, stuck in Carefree, Arizona, where his dad Jesse works as his school's janitor and tells drunken, embarrassing stories about having been a space cop. Then Jesse vanishes, and Sam finds the helmet — a real Nova helmet, with real power and no manual. Richard Rider is gone; the Corps is gone; what remains of the Nova legacy is a broke teenager learning on the job, all the way to the Champions.

primers.name: Destiny — Irene Adler
primers.text: Irene Adler died years before Krakoa: an elderly, blind precog who spent a century beside Mystique — her wife — recording her visions of mutantkind's possible futures in diaries the X-Men have chased ever since. She is the reason for Krakoa's strangest rule: *no precogs*. In one of Moira MacTaggert's past lives, Destiny saw the reincarnating woman's secret whole, told her exactly how many lives she had, and set terms Moira has obeyed ever since. Now the nation built on resurrection refuses to resurrect her, and Mystique keeps asking why. A dead woman who can see the future still holds cards in every negotiation on the island.

primers.name: The Midnight Mission — Supporting Cast (Soldier, Reese, Hunter's Moon)
primers.text: The Mission runs on its people. **Soldier**: a combat veteran who found the Mission — or was found by it — now its steady hands and its memory for who on the block needs help. **Reese**: the receptionist, a young vampire who chose this storefront over her own kind's politics; she works the desk, fields the desperate phone calls, and is frequently the most humane person in the building. **Hunter's Moon**: Dr. Yehya Badr, Khonshu's *other* Fist — where Marc Spector is chaos in a white suit, Badr is faith, discipline, and a physician's oath; a brother in everything except agreement. And **Tigra**, a veteran Avenger, keeps this strange little parish connected to the wider hero world. Broken people, protecting broken people, at 3 a.m.

primers.name: The Great Ring of Arakko — CONCEPT / TEAM
primers.text: Arakko is not governed; it is *held*. The Great Ring is the lost island's ruling council: nine seats, every one of them an omega-level mutant, divided among the tables of Dawn, Day, and Night — and each seat is kept the Arakki way, by being too strong for anyone to take. It is the Quiet Council's dark mirror: where Krakoa's council schemes in whispers, the Ring decides by open challenge, and a law is whatever survives the room. These are living weapons who spent millennia holding a breach against an endless demon invasion, now asked to be politicians. When the Ring speaks, two planets have to listen.

primers.name: Isca the Unbeaten
primers.text: Isca sits on the Great Ring, and her epithet is a literal description: her mutant gift makes it impossible for her to lose. In any conflict, her power bends *her* — allegiance included — toward the winning side, whether she wishes it or not. Her own people treat this as sacred law; everyone else experiences it as betrayal with a physics excuse. In *X of Swords* she takes the field as one of Arakko's champions, and both islands do the same cold arithmetic: wherever Isca ends up standing is where the war was always going to end. For Isca, loyalty is a weather report.

primers.name: Tarn the Uncaring
primers.text: Tarn the Uncaring is Arakko's gene-shaper: an omega-level master of living flesh who can rewrite a body — yours, his, an army's — with a gesture, growing weapons, monsters, and punishments out of meat. On the Great Ring he is less a politician than an institution: the one who decides what Arakki bodies are *for*. His entertainments run to cruelty and his standards to eugenics, and Storm's Mars is too small for both of them for long. When Tarn smiles at a visitor, something is about to be improved, in the Arakki sense of the word. It will not feel like an improvement.

primers.name: Lactuca the Knower
primers.text: Lactuca the Knower holds the Great Ring's quietest seat and its strangest omega gift: location. She knows where things *are* — every lost person, hidden weapon, and wandering god in creation has a place, and Lactuca perceives the universe as a vast song of positions, answering questions in fragments of it. In a culture that worships strength above all, she is revered purely for knowledge, which tells you how absolute that knowledge is. Arakko consults her the way other nations consult oracles: carefully, and only when they truly want the answer.

primers.name: The Ashen Combine
primers.text: When Kang comes to the Avengers begging (see primer 99), the Ashen Combine is part of what he is running from: a company of cosmic horrors — world-ending lords of strange domains, each one a catastrophe with a court — carried through space by the Impossible City, a sentient city-ship that is part vessel, part prison, part weapon. The City judges worlds; the Combine is what it keeps in the hold for the ones that fail. MacKay's *Avengers* opens with their arrival over Earth as the first of the Tribulation Events. Treat them the way the story does: not as villains to punch, but as weather from a worse universe. ---

primers.name: Black Widow — Natasha Romanoff
primers.text: Natasha Romanoff was the Soviet Union's finest product: a ballerina cover, a Red Room education, and a lifetime of missions she was never meant to remember clearly. She defected, became an Avenger, and built a second life in the West — but espionage doesn't retire its assets. *Homecoming*, where this primer anchors, finds her in Arizona when the past comes collecting, with a younger rival Widow, Yelena Belova, somewhere in the blast radius. Natasha is the guide's recurring reality check: the hero whose real superpower is knowing what everything costs.

primers.name: Quentin Quire — Kid Omega
primers.text: Quentin Quire is Xavier's most gifted student and its angriest: an omega-class telepath with a genius intellect, a punk revolutionary's aesthetic, and a crush on Magneto's oldest rhetoric. In "Riot at Xavier's," where this primer anchors, Quentin stops performing rebellion and starts one — drugs, manifestos, and a student uprising against everything the school claims to stand for. He is the first of this era's mutant radicals, asking why the dream's children should wait politely for a world that hates them. That question outlives the riot.

primers.name: Loki — God of Mischief (the original)
primers.text: Loki, Thor's adopted brother, is the god of mischief and the first villain the Avengers ever faced — a sorcerer and shapeshifter whose schemes run on resentment: Odin's favor, Thor's glory, a throne he believes his wit entitles him to. He died when Asgard fell, before this era began. In the returned Thor's new Oklahoma Asgard, Loki is back too — wearing the stolen form of Sif, smiling at his brother's table, playing a game whose horizon nobody else can see. With Loki, the question is never whether he's lying. It's who the lie is for.

primers.name: Adam Warlock
primers.text: Adam Warlock is a golden artificial human, grown in a cocoon by rogue scientists and reborn more than once since — a cosmic messiah figure who carried the Soul Gem and stood against Thanos when almost nobody else could. He also has a darkness built into his design: the Magus, his own future self turned god-tyrant, is the fate he exists to avoid. As *Annihilation: Conquest* opens, Warlock's cocoon hatches in the middle of the Phalanx war — and whatever wakes in his place is not behaving like the savior the galaxy remembers. ---

steps.label: [Era 02 §3.1] The Amazing Spider-Man (1999) #30–35, #36
steps.text: [Era 02 §3.1] The Amazing Spider-Man (1999) #30–35, #36 — JMS, "Coming Home" + "The Gift" — MUST-READ. The modern Peter: science teacher, Ezekiel and the totem mystery, Morlun.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.3] The Amazing Spider-Man (1999) #37–58, #500–518
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.3] The Amazing Spider-Man (1999) #37–58, #500–518 — JMS middle, best arcs only. Read the run's peaks; Sins Past (#509–514) is warn-and-skip per Era 02 §9.5 — know the retcon exists, don't read it.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Marvel Knights Spider-Man (2004) #1–12
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Marvel Knights Spider-Man (2004) #1–12 — Millar, "Down Among the Dead Men" + "Venomous" — EXPERT DEPTH. The better Spider-Man action book of 2004, concurrent with step 2.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5A] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 02 §5A] EVENT DIP — Avengers Disassembled (Era 02 §5A.2 core). Minimal context: the Avengers fall apart; Peter's own tie-in issues are aftermath blocks (§5A.3). Peter is a bystander here — the dip matters because it puts him on the New Avengers roster next.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5B.1] New Avengers (2004) #1–10
steps.text: [Era 02 §5B.1] New Avengers (2004) #1–10 — Peter joins the Avengers for the first time in his history. Team step, but a Peter milestone.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5B.8] Spider-Man: The Other
steps.text: [Era 02 §5B.8] Spider-Man: The Other — Amazing Spider-Man #525–528 + Marvel Knights Spider-Man #19–22 + Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man #1–4. Peter dies and comes back changed; the totem thread from step 1 pays off.

steps.label: [Era 02 §6] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 02 §6] EVENT DIP — House of M #1–8 core. Minimal context: in Wanda's rewritten world Peter got the life he always wanted (married, famous, Uncle Ben alive) — and remembers it afterward. That memory poisons everything in step 8.

steps.label: [Era 03 §2.3] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 03 §2.3] EVENT DIP — Civil War core order. Peter's biggest event role of the era: he unmasks on live TV as Iron Man's ally, then defects to Captain America's side. Read the full core at Era 03 §2.3; his solo tie-in issues slot inside it.

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.7] Amazing Spider-Man
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.7] Amazing Spider-Man — "Back in Black" → "One More Day" (2007). Context done honestly per the era file: Aunt May is shot because of the unmasking; Peter trades his marriage to Mephisto to save her. The marriage is gone from continuity from here on.

steps.label: [Era 03 §4.3] Amazing Spider-Man (1999) #546–647
steps.text: [Era 03 §4.3] Amazing Spider-Man (1999) #546–647 — Brand New Day, best arcs only (the guide cuts ~60 of 101 issues): #546–548 opener (status quo: broke, single, Harry alive, Mr. Negative debuts) · #568–573 "New Ways to Die" (MUST — Anti-Venom debuts) · #595–599 "American Son" (MUST — Harry vs. Norman, now the most powerful man alive) · Gauntlet selections #612–614 + #617 + #625 (Rhino) and #630–633 "Shed" (MUST — the Lizard, permanently) · #634–637 "Grim Hunt" (MUST — Kraven resurrected). Skip list with reasons at Era 03 §4.3/§11, including "One Moment in Time" (#638–641) — take a summary instead.

steps.label: [Era 03 §7.7] Amazing Spider-Man
steps.text: [Era 03 §7.7] Amazing Spider-Man — "Big Time" begins (2010–11), Slott's solo era, best arcs. Peter gets a science job and a real life; the run builds toward step 13.

steps.label: [Era 03 §8.7] Spider-Island
steps.text: [Era 03 §8.7] Spider-Island — Amazing Spider-Man #666–673 + sampled one-shots — EXPERT DEPTH-plus (borderline MUST for Spider-Man readers). All of Manhattan gets spider-powers; Peter's spider-sense is restored; Kaine is set up as Scarlet Spider (his own optional book is at Era 04 §7.5).

steps.label: [Era 04 §4.4] Superior Spider-Man (2013) #1–31 + Annuals
steps.text: [Era 04 §4.4] Superior Spider-Man (2013) #1–31 + Annuals — read COMPLETE, MUST for this track. Dying Doc Ock swaps minds with Peter and tries to prove himself the better Spider-Man: "My Own Worst Enemy" #1–5 → "A Troubled Mind" #6–10 → "No Escape" #11–16 → "Necessary Evil" #17–21 (Spider-Man 2099 stranded in the present — remember him) → "Superior Venom" #22–26 → "Goblin Nation" #27–31.

steps.label: [Era 04 §4.4] Spider-Verse (2014)
steps.text: [Era 04 §4.4] Spider-Verse (2014) — core complete, at Era 04 §4.4. Peter returns and leads every Spider-hero of the multiverse against the Inheritors. Minimal context: you need step 13 (Otto's role) and the Spider-Man 2099 support issues (Era 04 §7.5, OPTIONAL) only if Miguel is your draw.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H9] Amazing Spider-Man (2015) #789–801
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H9] Amazing Spider-Man (2015) #789–801 — Slott's finale: #789–791 "Fall of Parker Industries" (OPTIONAL — the CEO era ends, Peter is broke again) + #797–801 "Go Down Swinging" (STRONGLY — Red Goblin: Norman Osborn bonded to the Carnage symbiote; also your Carnage primer for Track 11).

steps.label: [Era 05 Block I7] The Amazing Spider-Man (2018) #1–45
steps.text: [Era 05 Block I7] The Amazing Spider-Man (2018) #1–45 — Nick Spencer, best + event-relevant arcs. A deliberate back-to-basics reset (Peter/MJ restored, roommate-era comedy) that slowly reveals Kindred — the era's long-game Spider-villain.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block I9] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL)
steps.text: [Era 05 Block I9] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL) — Spider-Geddon (2018) #0–5. The Inheritors return and are finished for good; Otto gets a final act Spencer's run references. Summary-safe.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.2] Amazing Spider-Man (2022) #1–60
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.2] Amazing Spider-Man (2022) #1–60 — Zeb Wells. Honest tiering from the era file: MUST for continuity, OPTIONAL for pleasure — key arcs only. The run's events (incl. the Gang War chapters and the Dark Web crossover, Era 06 §A8.3) move pieces the rest of the universe uses; the era file names which arcs to actually read.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.3] Amazing Spider-Man (2022) #61–70
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.3] Amazing Spider-Man (2022) #61–70 — "The 8 Deaths of Spider-Man" (Joe Kelly) — STRONGLY RECOMMENDED. Doom, now Sorcerer Supreme, delegates his annual duty — fighting Cyttorak's Scions — to Peter, with magic armour and eight resurrections. This is the Spider-Man/Doom bridge into One World Under Doom.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.3] Amazing Spider-Man (2025) #1–5
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.3] Amazing Spider-Man (2025) #1–5 — Kelly's relaunch — STRONGLY for the opening arc (Peter takes a job… in space; Norman Osborn as a supporting player), OPTIONAL ongoing; building toward legacy #1000.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.3] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.3] EVENT DIP — Death Spiral (Feb–May 2026), the nine-part Spider-Man/Venom crossover (order at Era 06 §B6.3). Shared with Track 11 — it is that track's on-ramp to its 2026 finale.

steps.label: [Era 02 §U / §3.5] SIDE TRACK
steps.text: [Era 02 §U / §3.5] SIDE TRACK — background only. Ultimate Spider-Man (2000) is Peter Parker's book, not Miles's. Read it (substantial cut at Era 02 §U) only to know the world Miles inherits. Miles himself: GAP — not created until 2011.

steps.label: [Era 03 Side Track A] SIDE TRACK. Ultimate Spider-Man (2000) #111–133 sampled + Ultimatum (MUST-for-this-track
steps.text: [Era 03 Side Track A] SIDE TRACK. Ultimate Spider-Man (2000) #111–133 sampled + Ultimatum (MUST-for-this-track, with the era file's explicit quality warning — the event is grim and weak, but it breaks this world and sets up everything after).

steps.label: [Era 03 Side Track A] SIDE TRACK. Ultimate Comics Spider-Man (2009) relaunch issues
steps.text: [Era 03 Side Track A] SIDE TRACK. Ultimate Comics Spider-Man (2009) relaunch issues — Peter's last Ultimate years; the world Miles is about to enter.

steps.label: [Era 03 Side Track A] SIDE TRACK
steps.text: [Era 03 Side Track A] SIDE TRACK — THE DEBUT. "The Death of Spider-Man": Ultimate Spider-Man #150–160 → **Ultimate Fallout #4 — Miles Morales's first appearance* → Ultimate Comics Spider-Man* (2011) #1–13 (Miles's origin run: a second spider, a reluctant kid, a world that just buried its Spider-Man).

steps.label: [Era 03 Side Track A] SIDE TRACK. Hickman's Ultimate Comics Ultimates
steps.text: [Era 03 Side Track A] SIDE TRACK. Hickman's Ultimate Comics Ultimates — included in this track for one reason: it is the origin of the Maker (Ultimate Reed Richards), who becomes a 616 villain and matters to Miles again in 2023+ (see step 12's note and Track 5).

steps.label: [Era 04 §8.1] SIDE TRACK
steps.text: [Era 04 §8.1] SIDE TRACK — the essential cut. Ultimate Comics: Spider-Man #1–12 (origin retold and deepened) → #13–18 "Venom strikes" (Miles's mother Rio dies — remember this for Secret Wars #9) → #23–28 → Cataclysm: Ultimate Spider-Man #1–3 (Era 04 §5.3) → #200 (a wake for Peter Parker) → Miles Morales: Ultimate Spider-Man #1–12, whose final pages are the direct on-ramp to Secret Wars #1.

steps.label: *[Era 04 §3.1] EVENT DIP
steps.text: *[Era 04 §3.1] EVENT DIP — Secret Wars (2015) #1–9 core.* Minimal context: both universes die; Miles survives on the life raft, gives Molecule Man a (very old) burger, and is written into the new 616 — with Rio alive again. Nobody, Miles included, knows at first. Full order at Era 04 §3.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block A4] All-New, All-Different Avengers (2015) #1–6
steps.text: [Era 05 Block A4] All-New, All-Different Avengers (2015) #1–6 — Miles on the flagship team alongside Ms. Marvel and Nova (Sam Alexander). The teen trio planted here walks out in step 11.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block A10] Spider-Man (2016) #1–5
steps.text: [Era 05 Block A10] Spider-Man (2016) #1–5 — Bendis/Pichelli — STRONGLY RECOMMENDED. Miles in 616: high school, the Avengers, his mother back. (Full run #1–21 + Annual OPTIONAL-STRONG; #6–10 is the Civil War II tie.)

steps.label: *[Era 05 Block D] EVENT DIP
steps.text: *[Era 05 Block D] EVENT DIP — Civil War II minimal core. Minimal context: a vision shows Miles standing over a dead Steve Rogers on the Capitol steps. It poisons the adult heroes' trust in him and is the direct cause of step 11 — and it pays off inverted in Secret Empire (Era 05 Block G2, the Uprising* one-shot).

steps.label: [Era 05 Block E1] Champions (2016) #1–5
steps.text: [Era 05 Block E1] Champions (2016) #1–5 — STRONGLY. Miles, Kamala and Nova quit the Avengers' model and found their own team. (Waid's full run is uneven — the era file's cut: #1–5, #13–15, then Jim Zub's Champions (2019) #1–10, the run experts rate highest.)

steps.label: [Era 05 Block I9] Miles Morales: Spider-Man (2018) #1–10
steps.text: [Era 05 Block I9] Miles Morales: Spider-Man (2018) #1–10 — Saladin Ahmed — STRONGLY for Miles readers. His Fresh Start solo: school, family, the Snatcher arc.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block K1] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL). Absolute Carnage
steps.text: [Era 05 Block K1] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL). Absolute Carnage — Miles's tie-in issues (#1–3) are the best of the event's tie-ins per the era file; the core event belongs to Track 11.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.3] Miles Morales: Spider-Man (2022) #1–…
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.3] Miles Morales: Spider-Man (2022) #1–… — Cody Ziglar — STRONGLY RECOMMENDED parallel Spider-book. Miles vs. Rabble; his Gang War chapters (Era 06 §B6.2 window); and a *core, not-immediately-undone consequence in Blood Hunt (Era 06 §B7): Miles is turned into a vampire.*

steps.label: [Era 06 Side Track S.4] SIDE-TRACK BRIDGE (OPTIONAL). Ultimate Spider-Man: Incursion (2025) #1–5
steps.text: [Era 06 Side Track S.4] SIDE-TRACK BRIDGE (OPTIONAL). Ultimate Spider-Man: Incursion (2025) #1–5 — the only bridge between Miles's 616 life and the new Ultimate Universe (Earth-6160) side track; also his road toward the Reborn: Ultimate Impact role noted at Era 06 §B6.3 (series ends Jan 2026 per the era file's live check).

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.1] New X-Men (2001) #114–154 + Annual 2001
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.1] New X-Men (2001) #114–154 + Annual 2001 — Grant Morrison, COMPLETE, MUST-READ. The modern X-Men start here: E is for Extinction (Genosha), the school as a school, Emma Frost, Xorn — and the Xorn/Magneto retcon problem is handled head-on at Era 02 §9.4.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.6] The other X-books of the Morrison years
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.6] The other X-books of the Morrison years — honest selections only: Uncanny X-Men #394–399 (Casey) and #410–415 (Austen's one good arc) at EXPERT DEPTH; X-Statix as a self-contained satire deep cut. Most of the concurrent line is cut, with reasons.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.8] The student books begin
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.8] The student books begin — New Mutants (2003) #1–13 → New X-Men: Academy X (2004) #1–15 (selection). The kids who Decimation (step 7) will hit hardest.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5B.2] Astonishing X-Men (2004) #1–12
steps.text: [Era 02 §5B.2] Astonishing X-Men (2004) #1–12 — Whedon/Cassaday begins: "Gifted" + "Dangerous." The flagship of the post-Morrison years.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5B.3] X-Men: Reload
steps.text: [Era 02 §5B.3] X-Men: Reload — the concurrent X-line selections that run beside step 4 (Claremont's Uncanny return begins at #444).

steps.label: *[Era 02 §6] EVENT
steps.text: *[Era 02 §6] EVENT — House of M #1–8 core + Group 1 tie-ins.* This is an X-event at its core: Wanda — a mutant, Magneto's daughter as then told — rewrites the world mutant-led, then ends it with "No more mutants." Full order at Era 02 §6.

steps.label: [Era 02 §7] DECIMATION
steps.text: [Era 02 §7] DECIMATION — full internal order. The X-line's defining status quo: ~198 mutants left. The Day After one-shot → X-Men (2004) #177–181 → Son of M #1–6 → New X-Men (2004) #20–27 ("Childhood's End"/"Crusade" — the student body is culled, brutally) → The 198 #1–5 → Generation M #1–5 → Sentinel Squad ONE #1–5 → X-Men: Deadly Genesis #1–6 → X-Factor (2005) #1–13 (Madrox's detective agency — the new normal's best book).

steps.label: [Era 02 §8.8–8.9] The 2006 relaunches + Astonishing X-Men #13–24 ("Torn" + "Unstoppable")
steps.text: [Era 02 §8.8–8.9] The 2006 relaunches + Astonishing X-Men #13–24 ("Torn" + "Unstoppable") — begins here, and its finale (Giant-Size Astonishing X-Men #1) lands at the start of the next era; do not leave the run unfinished.

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.9] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.9] EVENT — MESSIAH COMPLEX (2007–08), issue-level order. The first mutant baby since Decimation; every faction (X-Men, Marauders, Purifiers, Cable, Bishop) collides. The Messiah Trilogy's opening chapter — unanimous guide order at the cited section.

steps.label: [Era 03 §4.1] The X-books between events (Feb–Oct 2008)
steps.text: [Era 03 §4.1] The X-books between events (Feb–Oct 2008) — best-arcs bridge: the line regroups in San Francisco; Uncanny #500-era material and the satellite cuts are tiered here.

steps.label: [Era 03 §5.4] MESSIAH WAR + the road to Second Coming
steps.text: [Era 03 §5.4] MESSIAH WAR + the road to Second Coming — Cable/X-Force alternation in exact order (Era 03 §5.4). Hope, raised in the future by Cable, becomes the prize Bishop hunts across time.

steps.label: [Era 03 §7.2] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §7.2] EVENT — SECOND COMING (2010), issue-level. The Messiah Trilogy finale: Hope returns to the present; Bastion's final assault; Nightcrawler and Cable die making it matter.

steps.label: [Era 03 §7.3] Uncanny X-Force (2010) #1–35
steps.text: [Era 03 §7.3] Uncanny X-Force (2010) #1–35 — Remender, COMPLETE-RUN recommendation. Wolverine's kill-team; the Dark Angel Saga is broken out arc-by-arc at the citation. The best X-book of its years, and it seeds Era 04's Uncanny Avengers.

steps.label: [Era 03 §8.4] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §8.4] EVENT — SCHISM (2011) + REGENESIS. Wolverine and Cyclops split the species in two: Wolverine reopens the school (Wolverine & the X-Men), Cyclops militarises Utopia. Every X-book after this is on one side of that split.

steps.label: [Era 03 §9] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §9] EVENT — AVENGERS vs. X-MEN (2012), 20-step core. Prerequisites (all four keys at Era 03 §9.1) → main series #0–12 + only the tie-in arcs that change a main issue's meaning → AvX: Consequences #1–5 (the bridge into Era 04: Cyclops imprisoned, broken out, choosing revolution). Shared with Track 4 — it is both tracks' era finale.

steps.label: [Era 04 §6.1] Bendis X-Men
steps.text: [Era 04 §6.1] Bendis X-Men — best arcs, honestly tiered (NOT complete): Uncanny X-Men (2013) (Cyclops's revolution) + All-New X-Men (the original five X-Men, time-displaced into the present — the era's defining X-device). The era file names the arcs worth reading and the ones to cut.

steps.label: [Era 04 §6.2] The two Bendis-era crossovers, exact orders: Battle of the Atom and The Trial of Jean Grey (the
steps.text: [Era 04 §6.2] The two Bendis-era crossovers, exact orders: Battle of the Atom and The Trial of Jean Grey (the second is shared with Track 5 — the Guardians are the other half of it).

steps.label: [Era 04 §6.3] Uncanny Avengers (2012) #1–25
steps.text: [Era 04 §6.3] Uncanny Avengers (2012) #1–25 — Remender, COMPLETE ("it is one novel, and AXIS is its last act"). The Unity Squad; also Track 4's step — the two tracks genuinely share this book.

steps.label: [Era 04 §6.4] Wolverine's death arc
steps.text: [Era 04 §6.4] Wolverine's death arc — the short, complete path. Logan dies in 2014 and stays dead for years; Era 05's X-books are written in that absence (and Era 05 Side Track S1 imports Old Man Logan to fill the chair).

steps.label: [Era 04 §6.5] EVENT (OPTIONAL). The Black Vortex (2015), exact 13-part order at the citation if wanted
steps.text: [Era 04 §6.5] EVENT (OPTIONAL). The Black Vortex (2015), exact 13-part order at the citation if wanted — a Guardians/X-Men cosmic crossover; skippable without loss.

steps.label: *[Era 05 Block E4] EVENT
steps.text: *[Era 05 Block E4] EVENT — Death of X #1–4 + Inhumans vs. X-Men #0–6.* Minimal context the previous era deliberately withheld: what Cyclops actually did (and died doing) in the missing eight months, and the Terrigen war's resolution. The X-line's lowest ebb.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block M] THE HOLDING PATTERN (2016–2019)
steps.text: [Era 05 Block M] THE HOLDING PATTERN (2016–2019) — read the era file's triage, not the whole line. The keepers: Astonishing X-Men (2017) #1–12 (Soule) §M2 · X-Men Red (2018) #1–11 + Annual (Taylor — Jean Grey, back from the dead via Block H6 Phoenix Resurrection, leads the era's best X-book) §M3 · Extermination #1–5 §M4 (the time-displaced original five are sent home — step 16's device closes) · Uncanny X-Men (2018) #11–22 §M6 (Rosenberg's endgame clears the board). The ANAD launches (§M1) are SKIP-with-summary.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block N] ★ HOUSE OF X / POWERS OF X (2019)
steps.text: [Era 05 Block N] ★ HOUSE OF X / POWERS OF X (2019) — the Krakoa gateway. House of X #1–6 + Powers of X #1–6 in the era file's exact 12-issue interleave (HOX1, POX1, HOX2, POX2, POX3, HOX3, HOX4, POX4, HOX5, POX5, HOX6, POX6). Xavier, Magneto and Moira MacTaggert (a mutant, secretly, all along) found a mutant nation on Krakoa: resurrection, sovereignty, and a ten-lives conspiracy underneath it.

steps.label: [Era 06 Part A1] DAWN OF X (2019–20). The flagship X-Men (2019) #1–11 (Hickman) is MUST; the track's recommend
steps.text: [Era 06 Part A1] DAWN OF X (2019–20). The flagship X-Men (2019) #1–11 (Hickman) is MUST; the track's recommended rotation partners, tiered at Era 06 §A1: Marauders #1–12 · Excalibur #1–12 (becomes MUST for step 25) · X-Force #1–13 · Hellions #1–6 · X-Factor #1–3 · Wolverine (2020) #1–7. Fallen Angels is skip-safe — the era file says so.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A2] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §A2] EVENT — X OF SWORDS (2020), strict 22-chapter order. Krakoa vs. Arakko, the other half of the mutant world, in a tournament of blades. Excalibur and the Creation one-shots are load-bearing; the full chapter list is at the citation.

steps.label: [Era 06 Part A3] REIGN OF X (2020–21). X-Men (2019) #16–20 MUST; the line continues tiered (§A3.1–3.12): S.W.O
steps.text: [Era 06 Part A3] REIGN OF X (2020–21). X-Men (2019) #16–20 MUST; the line continues tiered (§A3.1–3.12): S.W.O.R.D. #1–11 (mutants take space — shared with Track 5), Hellions to #18, X-Factor to #10 + The Trial of Magneto #1–5, Way of X + Onslaught Revelation.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A4] HELLFIRE GALA #1 (2021) + INFERNO #1–4. The Gala terraforms Mars for Arakko
steps.text: [Era 06 §A4] HELLFIRE GALA #1 (2021) + INFERNO #1–4. The Gala terraforms Mars for Arakko — then Inferno is Hickman's exit: Moira's secret war with Xavier and Magneto detonates, Mystique and Destiny force the endgame, and Hickman leaves the line he built.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A5–A6] X LIVES / X DEATHS OF WOLVERINE (bridge) → DESTINY OF X, part 1. The new flagships: Immortal X
steps.text: [Era 06 §A5–A6] X LIVES / X DEATHS OF WOLVERINE (bridge) → DESTINY OF X, part 1. The new flagships: Immortal X-Men #1–4 (Gillen — the Quiet Council, Sinister's long game) + X-Men Red (2022) #1–4 (Ewing — Arakko/Mars) are both MUST; the rest of the line is tiered at §A6.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A7] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §A7] EVENT — A.X.E.: JUDGMENT DAY (2022). Shared with Tracks 4 and 12-adjacent (the Eternals are the third party). Prerequisites at §A7.0 are not optional — the era file is explicit. Strict core order at §A7.1: the Avengers' Celestial god judges every soul on Earth, and the X-Men's resurrection secret becomes public in the middle of it.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A8–A9] DESTINY part 2 → SINS OF SINISTER (2023), 11-issue event order. Sinister wins
steps.text: [Era 06 §A8–A9] DESTINY part 2 → SINS OF SINISTER (2023), 11-issue event order. Sinister wins — for a thousand years of corrupted timelines. Also in this window: Dark Web (§A8.3, the Spider-Man/X-Men bridge event — core only).

steps.label: [Era 06 §A10] BEFORE THE FALL + FALL OF X (2023). The trigger is one issue: X-Men: Hellfire Gala 2023 #1
steps.text: [Era 06 §A10] BEFORE THE FALL + FALL OF X (2023). The trigger is one issue: X-Men: Hellfire Gala 2023 #1 — Orchis attacks the Gala, Krakoa falls, mutants are scattered and outlawed. Read the MUST/RECOMMENDED blocks of the scattered line (§A10.3); the named skips are at §A10.4.

steps.label: *[Era 06 §A11] ★ THE KRAKOA FINALE
steps.text: *[Era 06 §A11] ★ THE KRAKOA FINALE — Fall of the House of X / Rise of the Powers of X (2024), strictly interleaved 19-step order, ending at X-Men #35 / Uncanny X-Men* #700. The five-year saga closes; read the two series as one book per the citation.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A12] FROM THE ASHES (2024–25)
steps.text: [Era 06 §A12] FROM THE ASHES (2024–25) — the post-Krakoa line. Three flagships, all MUST-tier as a set (any one alone is followable): MacKay's X-Men, Simone's Uncanny X-Men, Ewing's Exceptional X-Men; satellites tiered at §A12.2.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A13] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §A13] EVENT — AGE OF REVELATION (Oct–Dec 2025). A ten-years-later dark future event built on the From the Ashes status quo; core MUST, event-as-a-whole STRONGLY.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A14] SHADOWS OF TOMORROW (Jan 2026– )
steps.text: [Era 06 §A14] SHADOWS OF TOMORROW (Jan 2026– ) — the current line at guide cut-off. Flagships MUST, the rest tiered; ongoing.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.5] Avengers (1998) #41–76
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.5] Avengers (1998) #41–76 — selection. The last classic Avengers: the Kang war and the Busiek/Johns tail, read as the "before" picture.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5A] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 02 §5A] EVENT — AVENGERS DISASSEMBLED (2004). Core: Avengers #500–503 + Avengers Finale (prologue and aftermath blocks at §5A.1/§5A.3). Wanda, grieving and unravelled, destroys the team from inside. Everything in modern Marvel is downstream of this.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5A.4] Secret War (2004) #1–5
steps.text: [Era 02 §5A.4] Secret War (2004) #1–5 — Nick Fury's illegal Latveria op, staffed by future New Avengers; its blowback drives the team books for years.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5B.1] New Avengers (2004) #1–10
steps.text: [Era 02 §5B.1] New Avengers (2004) #1–10 — Bendis rebuilds the team from whoever is in the room: Cap, Iron Man, Spider-Man, Wolverine, Luke Cage, Spider-Woman, the Sentry.

steps.label: [Era 02 §8.1–8.2] New Avengers: Illuminati + New Avengers #11–25
steps.text: [Era 02 §8.1–8.2] New Avengers: Illuminati + New Avengers #11–25 — the Illuminati reveal (a secret cabal has steered everything — and exiled the Hulk; see Track 8) and the road into Civil War.

steps.label: [Era 03 §2.3] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §2.3] EVENT — CIVIL WAR (2006–07), 24-step core. The team splits down the middle over registration: Iron Man's pro-registration Avengers vs. Cap's underground. Full order at the citation; The Confession/The Return close it.

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.1] The split Avengers (2007)
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.1] The split Avengers (2007) — read the three launches together: New Avengers (the illegal team; #26–31 "Revolution" ends on the Elektra-is-a-Skrull page that starts the next event), Mighty Avengers (the official team), and the Illuminati (2007) mini (#1 and #5 MUST).

steps.label: [Era 03 §4.2] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §4.2] EVENT — SECRET INVASION (2008), 16-step core with flashback blocks. The Skrulls have replaced heroes for years. The era file's resolved call: read the reveal flashbacks as blocks, not interleaved — interleaving spoils the Veranke/Pym reveals.

steps.label: [Era 03 §5.1] DARK REIGN
steps.text: [Era 03 §5.1] DARK REIGN — the triad. Norman Osborn wins the invasion's peace and takes over: Dark Avengers (his team of villains-as-heroes), New Avengers (the resistance), Dark Reign: The List and satellites tiered at §5.2. An era, not an event — read it as a status quo.

steps.label: [Era 03 §5.3] Hickman arrives: Secret Warriors #1–28 (complete) + the FF prologue seeds. Fury's secret teams;
steps.text: [Era 03 §5.3] Hickman arrives: Secret Warriors #1–28 (complete) + the FF prologue seeds. Fury's secret teams; the writer who will own this track in Era 04 starts here.

steps.label: [Era 03 §7.1] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §7.1] EVENT — SIEGE (2010), 11 steps. Prerequisites at §6.3 are mandatory. Osborn invades Asgard and falls; the Dark Reign ends; the heroic age restarts.

steps.label: [Era 03 §7.6] The Heroic Age launches (2010–11): Avengers (2010) + New Avengers (2010) #1–6 (MUST
steps.text: [Era 03 §7.6] The Heroic Age launches (2010–11): Avengers (2010) + New Avengers (2010) #1–6 (MUST — Cage's bought-mansion team, and the magic-war arc that sets Era 04's Strange status) + Secret Avengers sampled. The new architecture: multiple Avengers teams, permanently.

steps.label: [Era 03 §8.2] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 03 §8.2] EVENT DIP — FEAR ITSELF (2011), main series sampled. The one tie-in promoted to MUST is Journey Into Mystery (Track 7's book). For this track the event is a Thor/Cap story; take the era file's sampled cut.

steps.label: [Era 03 §9] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §9] EVENT — AVENGERS vs. X-MEN (2012). Shared finale with Track 3 (see that track, step 15). Fallout: the Unity Squad forms (step 15 next era) and Xavier is dead.

steps.label: *[Era 04 §2.2] ★ THE HICKMAN SAGA
steps.text: *[Era 04 §2.2] ★ THE HICKMAN SAGA — Avengers + New Avengers + INFINITY, one strict interleave. The track's centrepiece, read issue-by-issue per §2.2: Phase A (Everything Dies / Avengers World) → Phase B: INFINITY (Thanos invades while the Avengers are off-world at war with the Builders) → Phase C (the fall, in parallel — Original Sin's mandatory piece is Avengers #29–34) → Phase D: TIME RUNS OUT (eight months later: Illuminati fugitive, Cap hunting them, the Cabal destroying worlds). Prerequisite: Hickman's Fantastic Four/FF* (Era 04 §2.1, full treatment owned by Era 03 §8.6's alternating order).

steps.label: [Era 04 §3.1] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 04 §3.1] EVENT — SECRET WARS (2015) #1–9. The incursions end both universes; Doom builds Battleworld; Reed rebuilds everything. The Last Days issues slot between Avengers #44 and Secret Wars #2 (Era 04 §3.2).

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.4] Mighty Avengers (2013) #1–14
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.4] Mighty Avengers (2013) #1–14 — Ewing — STRONGLY. Luke Cage's community Avengers (Monica Rambeau leads; Sam Wilson's first missions as Captain America). The era's warmest team book; starts inside Infinity.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block A2–A4] The ANAD launch trio: The Ultimates (2015) #1–12 (Ewing
steps.text: [Era 05 Block A2–A4] The ANAD launch trio: The Ultimates (2015) #1–12 (Ewing — the cosmic-scale problem-solvers; shared with Track 5) · New Avengers (2015) #1–6 (the Maker's first 616 move) · All-New, All-Different Avengers #1–6 (the flagship: Tony, Sam-Cap, Jane-Thor, Vision + the teen trio).

steps.label: [Era 05 Block B] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 05 Block B] EVENT — AVENGERS: STANDOFF! (2016), true 16-issue interleave. A small event with an outsized job: it restores Steve Rogers's youth — and plants the Kobik secret that becomes Secret Empire. Do not skip it; Track 9 depends on it.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block E2] Avengers (2016) #1–6
steps.text: [Era 05 Block E2] Avengers (2016) #1–6 — Waid's legacy-numbering run begins (the Kang war that scrambles the roster into the next launch).

steps.label: [Era 05 Block F3] Uncanny Avengers (2015) #18–23
steps.text: [Era 05 Block F3] Uncanny Avengers (2015) #18–23 — "Payoff": the Unity Squad's Red Skull conclusion (he still holds Xavier's brain). Closes step 18 of Track 3 / the Remender novel's last thread.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block G2] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 05 Block G2] EVENT — SECRET EMPIRE (2017), consensus 20-step core. Prerequisite chain is long and the era file enforces it: Standoff (step 19) → Captain America: Steve Rogers (Track 9, step 9) → the event. Steve, secretly rewritten by Kobik into a Hydra loyalist, takes America legally. The Avengers track supplies the resistance and the finale.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H1] Avengers: No Surrender
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H1] Avengers: No Surrender — Avengers (2016) #675–690. All three Avengers books merge for a weekly epic (the Grandmaster vs. the Challenger; Voyager's retcon debut). The Legacy era's team summit.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block I1] Avengers (2018) #1–17
steps.text: [Era 05 Block I1] Avengers (2018) #1–17 — Jason Aaron's run begins: the prehistoric Avengers, the Final Host of Celestials, Namor's war. Aaron's tenure runs years; the era file takes its launch + event-relevant arcs.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B5.1] Aaron's Avengers
steps.text: [Era 06 §B5.1] Aaron's Avengers — the finale block. Read after Judgment Day (step 26), as one block per the era file: the run's long threads (the multiversal Masters of Evil, Mephisto, the Avengers across time) converge.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A7] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 06 §A7] EVENT DIP — A.X.E.: JUDGMENT DAY (2022). Home treatment is Track 3 step 29; for this track the minimal context is: the Avengers are living inside a dead Celestial (Avengers Mountain) when their new god wakes up and judges the world — and the Avengers' own tie-in chapters are inside the strict core order at §A7.1.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B5.2] Avengers (2023) #1–36
steps.text: [Era 06 §B5.2] Avengers (2023) #1–36 — Jed MacKay — MUST (spine arcs) / STRONGLY (whole run). The modern flagship: Kang, the Twilight Court, the Ashen Combine — and the team that carries the next two events.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B7] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B7] EVENT — BLOOD HUNT (2024), strict 13-step core. MacKay's vampire event: the Darkforce dims the sun, Blade is possessed, and the Avengers are the front line. Fallout is immediate: Doom takes the Sorcerer Supreme mantle (Track 12) and Miles is turned (Track 2).

steps.label: [Era 06 §B8] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B8] EVENT — ONE WORLD UNDER DOOM (2025), strict 15-step core. Doom, holding Strange's stolen mantle, simply takes over the world — and runs it well enough that opposing him is the hard sell. The Avengers are the opposition's spine; the Fantastic Four book (Era 06 §B6.1) is the required partner read.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B9] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B9] EVENT — AVENGERS: ARMAGEDDON (Jun–Oct 2026) #1–5 — the current-era capstone. Prerequisites at §B9.1 (above all Zdarsky's Captain America (2025) — Track 9, step 13). The guide's endpoint at cut-off.

steps.label: [Era 02 §2.6] Marvel Boy (2000) #1–6
steps.text: [Era 02 §2.6] Marvel Boy (2000) #1–6 — Morrison's Noh-Varr. The Kree soldier who becomes a Krakoa-era player two decades later (Track 3, Era 06 §A6 window).

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Captain Marvel
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Captain Marvel — the Genis-Vell saga: Captain Marvel (1999) #0–6 → Captain Marvel (2002) #1–25 COMPLETE (EXPERT DEPTH). Genis, driven mad by cosmic awareness, becomes a cosmic menace; Phyla-Vell debuts in #16 — she matters in step 5.

steps.label: [Era 02 §8.5] The kindling: Thanos (2003) #7–12
steps.text: [Era 02 §8.5] The kindling: Thanos (2003) #7–12 — "Samaritan" (the arc's correct name; Era 02 QA correction) + the Drax setup. EXPERT but load-bearing for step 4.

steps.label: [Era 02 §8.6] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 02 §8.6] EVENT — ANNIHILATION (2006), complete internal order. The Annihilation Wave burns the Kree empire; Nova (Richard Rider) becomes the last Nova standing. The order (prologues → the four minis front-by-front → main series → Heralds) is uncontested across all the guide's sources.

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.6] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.6] EVENT — ANNIHILATION: CONQUEST (2007) + the NOVA LAUNCH. Read window: after World War Hulk (Era 03 §1.2 map). The Phalanx/Ultron conquer what's left; Nova (2007) launches out of it — DnA's run begins.

steps.label: *[Era 03 §4.6] ★ DnA COSMIC
steps.text: *[Era 03 §4.6] ★ DnA COSMIC — Nova #1–36 + Guardians of the Galaxy (2008) #1–25, COMPLETE. Read window: during/after Secret Invasion* on Earth (the era file's rule: cosmic runs concurrent with Earth events, never issue-interleaved with them — read in the windows, not the crossfire). The modern Guardians are founded here, in the ashes of two wars.

steps.label: [Era 03 §6.5] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §6.5] EVENT — WAR OF KINGS (2009). Read window: after the Dark Reign core. The Inhumans — now ruling the Kree — go to war with the Shi'ar; Guardians interleaves, Nova block-reads (the disagreement is stated and resolved at the citation). Black Bolt vs. Vulcan is the decade's best space-war climax.

steps.label: [Era 03 §6.6] Realm of Kings
steps.text: [Era 03 §6.6] Realm of Kings — the bridge chapter. Short; do not skip: the Fault (the tear War of Kings ripped in space) starts leaking a cancerverse.

steps.label: [Era 03 §7.5] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §7.5] EVENT — THE THANOS IMPERATIVE (2010). The DnA saga's finale: Thanos, death's avatar, is the only weapon against a universe where death lost. After this, the classic cosmic line goes quiet for years.

steps.label: [Era 04 §2.2, Phase B] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 04 §2.2, Phase B] EVENT DIP — INFINITY's space front (2013). Minimal context: while Thanos invades Earth, the Avengers join the Galactic Council against the Builders — the largest space war since step 9, and the track's only Era 04 event beat. Inside the spine order at the citation.

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.1] Guardians of the Galaxy (2013)
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.1] Guardians of the Galaxy (2013) — Bendis, best arcs only: #0.1 + #1–3 STRONGLY as an intro (movie-era relaunch; Iron Man joins). The era file is blunt: #14–27 drift (guest-star rotation without a story engine) and are skipped on a fast track — the DnA run in step 6 is the better Guardians book.

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.5] Silver Surfer (2014) #1–15
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.5] Silver Surfer (2014) #1–15 — Slott/Allred — STRONGLY RECOMMENDED, complete. Dawn Greenwood; the era's most joyful cosmic book. (Its #13–15 are post-Secret Wars "Last Days" placement — read them in the Era 05 window per the citation.)

steps.label: [Era 04 §5.6] Thanos Rising (2013)
steps.text: [Era 04 §5.6] Thanos Rising (2013) — OPTIONAL prequel to step 10 (Thanos's origin; split verdict stated at the citation).

steps.label: [Era 04 §6.5] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL). The Black Vortex (2015)
steps.text: [Era 04 §6.5] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL). The Black Vortex (2015) — the Guardians/X-Men crossover (Track 3, step 20). Cosmic readers take the exact order at the citation; everyone else skips.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block A2 + F4 + H9] ★ The Ultimates (2015) #1–12 → Ultimates 2 (2016) #1–6, #7–9, #100
steps.text: [Era 05 Block A2 + F4 + H9] ★ The Ultimates (2015) #1–12 → Ultimates 2 (2016) #1–6, #7–9, #100 — Al Ewing's cosmic saga, the era's cosmic spine. A team that solves cosmic problems before they reach Earth: Galactus is fixed (made a lifebringer), the cosmic jailer hierarchy is exposed, and the sequel's "Eternity War" frees Eternity from the First Firmament. STRONGLY throughout.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H9] Silver Surfer (2016) #1–14
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H9] Silver Surfer (2016) #1–14 — Slott/Allred — the completion of step 12's run (OPTIONAL-STRONG; Surfer readers treat Era 04 + this as one run). Includes the celebrated Möbius-strip issue #11.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H7] EVENT (OPTIONAL-MINIMAL
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H7] EVENT (OPTIONAL-MINIMAL — upgraded for this track). Infinity Countdown → Infinity Wars (2018). For most readers the era file tiers this OPTIONAL-MINIMAL; for cosmic/Guardians readers it is STRONGLY, because it is the finale of Duggan's Guardians of the Galaxy (2017) run (#146–150 + the All-New Guardians arcs — OPTIONAL-STRONG, and the event's only real prerequisite). Lasting facts: Thanos dies (for a while), the stones scatter, Warp World happens.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A3.2] S.W.O.R.D. (2020) #1–11
steps.text: [Era 06 §A3.2] S.W.O.R.D. (2020) #1–11 — Ewing — STRONGLY. Krakoa's space programme: mutants take over the orbital station, claim Mars/Arakko, and start arbitrating galactic politics. Shared with Track 3; this is where the X-line and the cosmic line merge.

steps.label: [Era 06 §A6.2] X-Men Red (2022) #1–4 → the Destiny-era continuation at §A8.2
steps.text: [Era 06 §A6.2] X-Men Red (2022) #1–4 → the Destiny-era continuation at §A8.2 — Ewing. Arakko (Mars) as a cosmic power: Storm regent of the Sol system, Brand's long con, Vulcan returned. MUST within the Krakoa saga; for this track it is the 2022–24 cosmic flagship.

steps.label: [Era 06 §0 spine] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 06 §0 spine] EVENT DIP — EMPYRE (2020). The Kree/Skrull alliance (Hulkling, emperor) vs. the Cotati — the space-empires status quo Imperial later detonates. Home treatment is the backbone (01, Ch 21→22 window) and Era 06's spine summary; read it before step 21.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B8.3] ★ EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B8.3] ★ EVENT — IMPERIAL (2025) #1–4 — Hickman — STRONGLY RECOMMENDED (cosmic spine). The empires (Kree/Skrull, Shi'ar, Wakanda's intergalactic empire, Nova) are manoeuvred into a new galactic order — deliberately built as the launchpad for a new cosmic line, and the reason this track ends on an upswing.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B8] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 06 §B8] EVENT DIP — ONE WORLD UNDER DOOM (2025). Doom's takeover is Earth-first, but its cosmic clauses (the mantle, the empires' recognition of his rule) are set inside the strict order at the citation; read after step 21.

character_tracks.name: STREET-LEVEL (Daredevil / Punisher / Moon Knight / Jessica Jones)

steps.label: [Era 02 §2.2] Daredevil (1998) #1–8
steps.text: [Era 02 §2.2] Daredevil (1998) #1–8 — "Guardian Devil" (Kevin Smith). The Marvel Knights relaunch; Mysterio's last game breaks Matt.

steps.label: [Era 02 §2.3] Daredevil (1998) #9–15
steps.text: [Era 02 §2.3] Daredevil (1998) #9–15 — "Parts of a Hole." Echo debuts; the Kingpin machinery resets for the Bendis years.

steps.label: [Era 02 §3.2] Daredevil (1998) #16–19
steps.text: [Era 02 §3.2] Daredevil (1998) #16–19 — "Wake Up" (Bendis). A child, a coma, and Leap-Frog — the tone of the coming run in miniature.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.2] Daredevil (1998) #26–81
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.2] Daredevil (1998) #26–81 — Bendis, COMPLETE, MUST-READ. Matt's identity is outed to the FBI and the press, and the run never lets him take it back: the trial, the marriage, the Kingpin's fall and return, the White Tiger case. The defining Daredevil run of the modern age.

steps.label: [Era 02 §8.7] Daredevil (1998) #82–93
steps.text: [Era 02 §8.7] Daredevil (1998) #82–93 — Brubaker begins ("The Devil in Cell-Block D"): Matt in prison, framed, while someone else wears the horns (Danny Rand — remember him for Era 03's Iron Fist launch).

steps.label: [Era 03 §4.4] Brubaker's run concludes + the road to Shadowland: Matt takes over the Hand to keep it from wors
steps.text: [Era 03 §4.4] Brubaker's run concludes + the road to Shadowland: Matt takes over the Hand to keep it from worse hands — the era file's honest arc-by-arc tiering applies; the Diggle handoff is where quality thins.

steps.label: [Era 03 §7.4] EVENT-ADJACENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §7.4] EVENT-ADJACENT — SHADOWLAND (2010). Daredevil falls: possessed, ruling Hell's Kitchen from a fortress, killed by Bullseye's hand through his own. The era file's call stands: skippable for spine readers, with its summary paragraph carrying the facts — but for this track it is the run's ending and should be read.

steps.label: [Era 04 §4.3] Daredevil
steps.text: [Era 04 §4.3] Daredevil — Mark Waid, COMPLETE for the era. The deliberate inversion: a swashbuckling, happy Matt (who is lying to himself, and the run knows it). Foggy's cancer arc is the run's heart.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H9] Daredevil (2015) #595–612
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H9] Daredevil (2015) #595–612 — Soule's conclusion: #595–605 "Mayor Fisk" (STRONGLY — Fisk is elected Mayor of New York and outlaws vigilantism) + #606–612 "The Death of Daredevil." Both are required context for step 10 — the era file says so explicitly.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block L1–L2] Man Without Fear (2019) #1–5 (bridge) → Daredevil (2019) #1–25
steps.text: [Era 05 Block L1–L2] Man Without Fear (2019) #1–5 (bridge) → Daredevil (2019) #1–25 — Chip Zdarsky begins ★. Matt, back from near-death, kills a criminal by accident in his first fight back — and the run is the working-out of that guilt, against Mayor Fisk's New York.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B3.1] Daredevil (2019) #26–36
steps.text: [Era 06 §B3.1] Daredevil (2019) #26–36 — Zdarsky concludes the run (the era file reads the full #1–36 as MUST; Era 05 owns #1–25, this file picks up at #26 — do not re-read). Matt goes to prison as Daredevil; Elektra takes the horns in his place.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B3.2] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B3.2] EVENT — DEVIL'S REIGN (2021) #1–6 + Omega. Zdarsky/Checchetto. Fisk, as Mayor, outlaws superheroes outright and runs his Thunderbolts on the city — the Mayor Fisk thread (steps 9–11) detonates. MUST-READ EVENT for this track.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B3.3] Daredevil (2022) #1–14
steps.text: [Era 06 §B3.3] Daredevil (2022) #1–14 — "The Red Fist Saga" — Zdarsky's finale: Matt and Elektra (both Daredevils now) build an army against the Hand, whose true nature finally surfaces.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B3.4] After Zdarsky
steps.text: [Era 06 §B3.4] After Zdarsky — tiered honestly at the citation. The post-Zdarsky relaunch is a step down the era file does not hide; read it as a coda, not a pillar.

steps.label: [Era 02 §2.4] Punisher (2000) #1–12
steps.text: [Era 02 §2.4] Punisher (2000) #1–12 — "Welcome Back, Frank" (Ennis). The Knights relaunch that rescued the character from the angelic-Punisher years.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Punisher (2001) #1–37
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Punisher (2001) #1–37 — Ennis, EXPERT DEPTH selections ("Army of One," "Business as Usual," "Streets of Laredo"). The 616 Ennis run, read in the main order.

steps.label: *[Era 02 Side Track, §4 anchor] SIDE TRACK
steps.text: *[Era 02 Side Track, §4 anchor] SIDE TRACK — Punisher MAX (2004) #1–60, Ennis (Earth-200111).* The definitive Punisher run, fenced out of 616 on purpose: "The Slavers" (#25–30) is its most acclaimed arc. Window: any time after Era 02 §3; zero interaction with the main order.

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.5] The soldier books under the events (2006–08): Fraction's Punisher War Journal
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.5] The soldier books under the events (2006–08): Fraction's Punisher War Journal — Frank inside Civil War/Dark Reign continuity (his Captain America obsession in Civil War is the character beat; the era file tiers the arcs).

steps.label: [Era 03 §5.5] Remender's Punisher
steps.text: [Era 03 §5.5] Remender's Punisher — best-arcs honesty: the run that kills Frank and rebuilds him as Franken-Castle. Read the era file's selected arcs; the premise is better than its reputation and worse than its fans claim.

steps.label: [Era 03 §8.7] Rucka's Punisher (2011)
steps.text: [Era 03 §8.7] Rucka's Punisher (2011) — sampled in the era's street/solo best-of: a silent, procedural Frank and the best Punisher writing of the Bendis era's tail.

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.5] Punisher (2014) #1–20
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.5] Punisher (2014) #1–20 — Edmondson — OPTIONAL (solid Frank-vs.-L.A. run); its #19–20 are the Secret Wars "Last Days" issues (Era 04 §3.2) and explain his event cameo.

steps.label: GAPS (honest): No Punisher solo makes the main guide's cut in Era 05 or Era 06. Frank appears at event margins
steps.text: GAPS (honest): No Punisher solo makes the main guide's cut in Era 05 or Era 06. Frank appears at event margins (and the MAX side track, step 3, remains the character's best long-form read in the whole guide). The 2022 Aaron Punisher run is not in the main guide — flagged here so its absence is a decision, not an oversight.

steps.label: [Era 02 §8.10] Moon Knight (2006) #1–6
steps.text: [Era 02 §8.10] Moon Knight (2006) #1–6 — "The Bottom" (Huston/Finch) — EXPERT DEPTH. Marc Spector, broken at the bottom of a staircase, Khonshu calling. The first arc is the keeper; the 2006 series continues unevenly (era file's verdict).

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — Era 03: no Moon Knight solo in the main guide's cut (he is a Secret Avengers presence at event margins). Honest gap.

steps.label: [Era 04 §4.8] Moon Knight (2014)
steps.text: [Era 04 §4.8] Moon Knight (2014) — the Ellis six, COMPLETE (#1–6, Warren Ellis/Declan Shalvey: Mr. Knight, done-in-one cases); the rest of the volume honestly tiered at the citation (Wood's and Bunn's arcs are a step down).

steps.label: [Era 05, QA Pass 2 additions] Moon Knight (2016) #1–14
steps.text: [Era 05, QA Pass 2 additions] Moon Knight (2016) #1–14 — Jeff Lemire, COMPLETE. Marc in an asylum that may be Khonshu's trap; the character's definitive modern statement, added to the guide in QA Pass 2 after Pass 1 missed it.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B4.1] Moon Knight (2021) #1–30
steps.text: [Era 06 §B4.1] Moon Knight (2021) #1–30 — Jed MacKay — MUST-READ. The Midnight Mission: Marc, therapised and terrifying, protects travellers of the night — and builds the supporting cast (Reese, Soldier, Hunter's Moon) the rest of the sequence runs on.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B4.2] Vengeance of the Moon Knight (2024) #1–9
steps.text: [Era 06 §B4.2] Vengeance of the Moon Knight (2024) #1–9 — MUST (continuation, not a reboot). Marc is dead (in Blood Hunt's run-up the era file places it here); someone else is wearing the white — the Mission holds the line while the truth surfaces.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B4.3] Moon Knight: Fist of Khonshu (2024) #0–15
steps.text: [Era 06 §B4.3] Moon Knight: Fist of Khonshu (2024) #0–15 — STRONGLY. Marc returned; the MacKay sequence's third act. (Rotation note at Era 06 §B4: these Moon Knight chunks interleave with the Strange sequence — Track 12 — in the main order's Cluster R4; the two tracks are neighbours by design.)

steps.label: [Era 02 §3.3] Alias (2001) #1–28
steps.text: [Era 02 §3.3] Alias (2001) #1–28 — COMPLETE, MUST-READ. Bendis's MAX-line detective book: a failed ex-hero (Jewel) drinking her way through other people's cases, ending at the Purple Man — the most acclaimed street-level book of its decade, and Jessica's entire foundation.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] The Pulse (2004) #1–14
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] The Pulse (2004) #1–14 — EXPERT DEPTH selections (#1–5 + #11–14). Alias's newspaper-set sequel: Jessica at the Bugle, pregnant by Luke Cage; the Secret War fallout issues (#6–9) read after Era 02 §5A.4.

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — Era 03 to mid-Era 04: no Jessica solo in the main guide. She is a New Avengers regular (Track 4, steps 4–12 — her marriage to Luke and Danielle's birth happen there) and a Secret War/Civil War margin presence. The track's honest centre of gravity in these years is the team book.

steps.label: [Era 05, QA Pass 2 additions] Jessica Jones (2016) #1–18
steps.text: [Era 05, QA Pass 2 additions] Jessica Jones (2016) #1–18 — Bendis returns to his creation: Jessica is out of prison, her marriage is (apparently) wrecked, and the case is why. Added in QA Pass 2; the Purple Man sequel arc closes the Alias thread.

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — Era 06: no Jessica Jones solo in the main guide's cut. She appears at street/event margins (Devil's Reign's New York is her neighbourhood — Track 6 readers will meet her there), but the track's last full step is step 4.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Thor (1998) #68–79
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Thor (1998) #68–79 — Jurgens, "The Reigning" build — COMPLETIONIST run, one EXPERT arc: read this selection so that step 2 hurts. (The volume's earlier arcs are skippable without loss.)

steps.label: [Era 02 §5A] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 02 §5A] EVENT DIP — Disassembled's Thor front: RAGNAROK. Thor's own Disassembled tie-in (Thor #80–85) is where the Avengers' collapse and Asgard's end are the same story. Thor and Asgard die here — which is why step 3 exists.

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — 2004–2007: Thor is dead. Era 03 §2.4 is titled for it ("Thor is dead (for now) — a deliberate absence"). A fake Thor (the cyborg clone Ragnarok) is a Civil War beat — see it inside Track 4, step 6; there is no Thor book to read.

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.8] Thor (2007) #1–12 + #600–603
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.8] Thor (2007) #1–12 + #600–603 — JMS. Thor returns, resurrects Asgard — floating over Oklahoma — and refuses every easy reconciliation with Tony Stark (the clone is not forgiven). The modern Asgard-on-Earth status quo starts here.

steps.label: [Era 03 §5.7] Thor #604–614
steps.text: [Era 03 §5.7] Thor #604–614 — Gillen's stewardship (2009–10). The Siege bridge: Doom's Asgardian experiments, Kelda, and the pieces Siege (Track 4, step 11 — Thor's homecoming event) spends.

steps.label: [Era 03 §8.2] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §8.2] EVENT — FEAR ITSELF (2011), with the tie-in promoted to MUST. The main series is sampled for most tracks; for this one, read it with **Journey Into Mystery #622–645 — Gillen, COMPLETE** — the era file promotes JIM over the event it ties into: kid-Loki, resurrected wrong and trying to be good, secretly fights the Serpent war the adults are losing loudly. It is also Loki's essential modern book.

steps.label: [Era 03 §8.3] Thor after Fear Itself: Fraction's The Mighty Thor is demoted by the era file against JMS/Gillen
steps.text: [Era 03 §8.3] Thor after Fear Itself: Fraction's The Mighty Thor is demoted by the era file against JMS/Gillen — sampled, not prescribed. Honest step: the book exists, the guide cuts it, the Aaron era (step 8) is where the track's weight sits.

steps.label: *[Era 04 §4.1] ★ Thor: God of Thunder (2012) #1–25
steps.text: *[Era 04 §4.1] ★ Thor: God of Thunder (2012) #1–25 — Jason Aaron, read COMPLETE.* "The God Butcher" #1–5 + Gorr's origin #6 + "Godbomb" #7–11 (three Thors — young, present, King Thor — hunt a god-killer across time; one of the great Thor stories, full stop) → #12 (Roz Solomon debuts) → "The Accursed" #13–17 (Malekith returns — plant him for step 13) → #18 → "The Last Days of Midgard" #19–24 → #25 epilogue.

steps.label: *[Era 04 §5.4] EVENT DIP
steps.text: *[Era 04 §5.4] EVENT DIP — Original Sin #7 (one issue, mandatory for this track). Fury whispers an unknown secret to Thor. Thor becomes unworthy*, mid-battle, and drops Mjolnir on the Moon. Nobody — reader included — learns what was said for years.

steps.label: [Era 04 §4.1] Thor (2014) #1–8
steps.text: [Era 04 §4.1] Thor (2014) #1–8 — "Goddess of Thunder." A woman lifts the hammer while Odinson investigates, re-arms with the axe Jarnbjorn, and loses an arm. Her identity is revealed in #8 and is earned — do not let it be spoiled. (Thor Annual (2015) #1 OPTIONAL.)

steps.label: [Era 05 Thor Thread
steps.text: [Era 05 Thor Thread — Blocks A7/C3/F4/H2] The Mighty Thor (2015) #1–23 + The Unworthy Thor (2016) #1–5, read in the era file's thread order (Parts A–C interleaved with the era's events, not binged): Jane Foster, dying of cancer, is Thor — and every transformation kills the chemotherapy keeping her alive. Unworthy Thor runs beside it: Odinson, offered a dead world's hammer (the Ultimate Thor's — a Secret Wars leftover), refuses it.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H2] Thor Thread Part C conclusion: Generations: The Thunder (2017) #1 → The Mighty Thor #700–706
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H2] Thor Thread Part C conclusion: Generations: The Thunder (2017) #1 → The Mighty Thor #700–706 — "The Death of the Mighty Thor" → Mighty Thor: At the Gates of Valhalla (2018) #1. Jane's arc ends the way it was always going to; read the era file's ordering, not the trade order.

steps.label: *[Era 05 Block I4 + Block J] ★ Thor (2018) #1–11 → WAR OF THE REALMS (2019) → King Thor #1–4
steps.text: *[Era 05 Block I4 + Block J] ★ Thor (2018) #1–11 → WAR OF THE REALMS (2019) → King Thor #1–4 — Aaron's finale. The event (core order at Block J1) is the payoff of the whole Aaron saga: Malekith's decade-long conquest (planted at step 8) reaches Earth; every Thor thread — Jane, Odinson, King Thor, Loki, the Thor Corps of futures — converges. King Thor* is the saga's true ending, set at the end of time.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.4] Thor (2020) #1–35
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.4] Thor (2020) #1–35 — Cates (to #23) / Grønbekk — OPTIONAL, honestly tiered: the Black Winter, Galactus's death, Donald Blake. Good and self-contained; its King in Black tie-ins (#7–9) belong to Track 11's optional set.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.4] Immortal Thor (2023) #1–25
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.4] Immortal Thor (2023) #1–25 — Al Ewing — STRONGLY RECOMMENDED (deep cut). "Read Immortal Thor if you read any solo Thor in this era" (era file's words): mythic, literary Thor against the Utgard gods and Roxxon's Dario Agger, with a meta-narrative engine. Ends 2025 handing Thor toward a mortal-rebirth status quo (Thor (2025), Ahmed — OPTIONAL, ongoing).

steps.label: [Era 06 §B2.5] EVENT DIP (one-shot). Queen in Black: Thor #1 (2026)
steps.text: [Era 06 §B2.5] EVENT DIP (one-shot). Queen in Black: Thor #1 (2026) — the Thor chapter of Track 11's finale event; read inside that event's core order at the citation.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Incredible Hulk (1999) #34–39
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Incredible Hulk (1999) #34–39 — Bruce Jones, "Return of the Monster" (EXPERT DEPTH selections). Banner on the run, conspiracy tone. (Skip Jones's middle per §10; then *Peter David's Tempest Fugit #77–82* resets Hulk psychology before step 3.)

steps.label: [Era 02 §6] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL). The House of M Hulk tie-in issues (#83–86 + coda)
steps.text: [Era 02 §6] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL). The House of M Hulk tie-in issues (#83–86 + coda) — Hulk as Australia's governor in Wanda's world. Colour, not load-bearing.

steps.label: [Era 02 §8.3–8.4] ★ PLANET HULK
steps.text: [Era 02 §8.3–8.4] ★ PLANET HULK — complete, one block. Prelude: Incredible Hulk #88–91 ("Peace in Our Time") + Fantastic Four #533–535 → Incredible Hulk #92–105 + Giant-Size Hulk (2006) #1 (after #95). The Illuminati exile Hulk (Track 4, step 5 — the betrayal is the point); on Sakaar he becomes gladiator, then king, then husband — and the ship that brought him explodes. Placement note: Era 03 §2.2 holds the arbitration — the block sits concurrent with Civil War, split around it in the main order's window model; in this track, read it whole.

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.4] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.4] EVENT — WORLD WAR HULK (2007). Hulk comes home with an army and a list. The Illuminati answer for step 3, one by one; the Sentry fight levels Manhattan; the ending (Miek's betrayal, Hulk's surrender) sets up the entire post-war Hulk line.

steps.label: [Era 03 §4.5] Hulk after World War Hulk
steps.text: [Era 03 §4.5] Hulk after World War Hulk — the Pak/Loeb split, best-arcs honesty: Pak's continuation (the Skaar thread, step 6) is the keeper; Loeb's Red Hulk mystery is sampled to #1–6 + the Fall of the Hulks reveals only (Era 03 §7.8) — the era file names the rest as skips.

steps.label: [Era 03 §6.7] Skaar comes to Earth
steps.text: [Era 03 §6.7] Skaar comes to Earth — the Hulk-line bridge: the son Hulk never knew, raised on Sakaar, arrives hunting his father.

steps.label: [Era 03 §5.6] Incredible Hercules
steps.text: [Era 03 §5.6] Incredible Hercules — best arcs (Hulk-family adjacent). Amadeus Cho — the kid who was right about Hulk in step 4 — headlines the era's best comedy-adventure book with Hercules. OPTIONAL for the track, STRONGLY as a comic.

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.5] Indestructible Hulk (2012) #1–20
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.5] Indestructible Hulk (2012) #1–20 — Waid — OPTIONAL, #1–8 is its best (Banner weaponises the Hulk for S.H.I.E.L.D. — "Hulk destroys, Banner builds"). Then Hulk (2014) #1–4 (Waid: "Banner D.O.A." — Banner shot in the head, saved by Tony with Extremis) + #5–16 (Duggan, "Doc Green") — OPTIONAL, Hulk fans only. The era file's grading is the honest one: decent runs a fast track cannot afford at full length.

steps.label: [Era 04 §5.4] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL but consequential). Original Sin: Hulk vs. Iron Man #3.1–3.4. The spilt secr
steps.text: [Era 04 §5.4] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL but consequential). Original Sin: Hulk vs. Iron Man #3.1–3.4. The spilt secret: Tony's drunken hand in the gamma bomb's targeting. It reframes Hulk/Iron Man relations and feeds Tony's Era 04 isolation (Track 10).

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — 2015–2018: Bruce Banner is dead. Killed by Hawkeye during Civil War II (Era 05 Block D — the trial fallout is The Fallen #1, Block D2). In the interval the Hulk chair is held by Amadeus Cho (the Totally Awesome Hulk — find him in Champions, Track 2 step 11's book) and by Jen Walters's darker Hulk run, which the main guide does not carry. The track states the gap rather than filling it.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block I2] ★★ THE IMMORTAL HULK (2018) #1–50
steps.text: [Era 05 Block I2] ★★ THE IMMORTAL HULK (2018) #1–50 — Ewing, COMPLETE RUN. The track's summit and one of the guide's crown jewels: a horror book — Banner dies by day, the Devil Hulk walks by night, and the Green Door opens onto the One Below All. The era file's placement: it begins in Fresh Start (Block I) and its back half runs into the next era (step 12) — do not stop at the era seam.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B1] Immortal Hulk
steps.text: [Era 06 §B1] Immortal Hulk — THE FINISH (2020–21). Era 06 picks the run up where Era 05's portion ends (the files' pointer convention: Era 05 carries the front, Era 06 §B1 carries the conclusion through #50 — the Xemnu arc, the Leader's endgame, the final door). Read straight through the seam.

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — post-2021 (honest): no Hulk solo makes the main guide's spine after Immortal Hulk — the Cates and Johnson runs are not in the guide's cut. Banner/Hulk appear at event margins (notably the One World Under Doom window, Era 06 §B8) but the track's last full step is step 12. The guide flags this as its own open item rather than a verdict on those runs.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Truth: Red, White & Black (2003) #1–7
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Truth: Red, White & Black (2003) #1–7 — MUST-READ. Isaiah Bradley: Black soldiers experimented on before Steve Rogers. It feeds Brubaker's run, Young Avengers (Eli Bradley is Isaiah's grandson — step 4), and every modern Cap conversation. Read it before step 3.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Captain America (2002) #1–32
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Captain America (2002) #1–32 — Marvel Knights, EXPERT DEPTH selections: Rieber's "The New Deal" #1–6 (post-9/11 Cap). The volume is mixed and Brubaker restarts the title in 2005 — do not grind all 32.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5B.4] Captain America (2005) #1–14
