steps.text: [Era 02 §5B.4] Captain America (2005) #1–14 — Brubaker begins. "Out of Time" + "Winter Soldier": a Soviet assassin with a metal arm is killing Brubaker-era loose ends, and he is Bucky Barnes. The defining modern Cap run starts here.

steps.label: [Era 02 §5B.6] Young Avengers (2005) #1–12 + Special
steps.text: [Era 02 §5B.6] Young Avengers (2005) #1–12 + Special — team dip for this track: Patriot (step 1's payoff), and the next generation assembling in Cap's absence-to-come.

steps.label: [Era 03 §2.1] Captain America (2005) #15–24 (this era's portion of the run)
steps.text: [Era 03 §2.1] Captain America (2005) #15–24 (this era's portion of the run) — read BEFORE Civil War per the era file (these issues feed the event directly: the Red Skull/Lukin endgame, Sharon Carter's compromise).

steps.label: [Era 03 §2.3] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 03 §2.3] EVENT DIP — CIVIL WAR core. Steve leads the anti-registration underground and surrenders on the courthouse steps to end the fighting. His tie-in issues are inside the 24-step core at the citation.

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.3] ★ THE DEATH OF CAPTAIN AMERICA (2007–08). Captain America (2005) #25–42 in the era file's order:
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.3] ★ THE DEATH OF CAPTAIN AMERICA (2007–08). Captain America (2005) #25–42 in the era file's order: Steve is assassinated on those same steps; the Skull's plot runs through Sharon and Faustus; Bucky Barnes takes the shield — first to avenge, then to deserve it.

steps.label: [Era 03 §6.1] Captain America: Reborn + the Bucky-Cap endgame: Steve returns (his consciousness was unstuck in
steps.text: [Era 03 §6.1] Captain America: Reborn + the Bucky-Cap endgame: Steve returns (his consciousness was unstuck in time, not dead — the era file gives the honest mechanics), and chooses to let Bucky keep the shield while he runs S.H.I.E.L.D.

steps.label: [Era 03 §8.5] Cap 2011: "The Trial of Captain America" + Brubaker's Steve vol. 6 (best arcs only
steps.text: [Era 03 §8.5] Cap 2011: "The Trial of Captain America" + Brubaker's Steve vol. 6 (best arcs only — the era file names #6–10/#15–19 as skips) + Winter Soldier (2012) launch (Bucky back in the shadows, where he works best).

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.4] Captain America (2012) #1–25
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.4] Captain America (2012) #1–25 — Remender, best arcs: #1–10 "Dimension Z" STRONG (Cap raises a son inside Zola's dimension for a decade of subjective time) · #11–19 OPTIONAL · #21–25 STRONGLY for continuity: the Iron Nail drains the super-soldier serum → Steve ages into an old man → the shield passes to Sam Wilson. Then All-New Captain America #1–6 OPTIONAL (Sam's first arc; its Hydra infiltration plot pays off notoriously in Era 05).

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.4] Mighty Avengers (2013) #1–14
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.4] Mighty Avengers (2013) #1–14 — Sam Wilson's first missions as Captain America are here (inside Track 4, step 17). Read the STRONGLY portion if Sam is your Cap.

steps.label: [Era 04 §2.2, Phases C–D] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 04 §2.2, Phases C–D] EVENT DIP — the spine's Cap. Old Steve, commanding from a chair, becomes the Illuminati's hunter in Time Runs Out — the moral inversion (Cap as the saga's antagonist, and not wrong) is the Hickman saga's engine. He and Tony die together in the final incursion (Era 04 §3.1) — and both are simply alive in Era 05; Steve's restoration is step 13, Tony's is never dramatised (the era files flag this so you don't hunt for a missing issue).

steps.citation: Era 05 Block B + C + F + G
steps.label: [Era 05 Block B + C + F + G] ★ THE SECRET EMPIRE ARC
steps.text: [Era 05 Block B + C + F + G] ★ THE SECRET EMPIRE ARC — read as one chain, in this order: Avengers: Standoff! (Block B — Kobik, the sentient Cosmic Cube child, restores Steve's youth and secretly rewrites him) → Captain America: Steve Rogers #1–6 (Block C1 — "Hail Hydra") → the Steve Rogers/Sam Wilson interleave (Blocks C2/F1 — two Captain Americas, one country splitting) → **Secret Empire core* (Block G2, consensus 20-step order). The most controversial Cap story ever published; the guide's position is that the buildup is* the story and the event only works read whole.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H3] Tales of Suspense (2017) #100–104
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H3] Tales of Suspense (2017) #100–104 — "Red Ledger." Bucky and Natasha, post-Secret Empire, hunting what the fallout left behind. The Brubaker era's true coda.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H9] Captain America (2017) #695–704
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H9] Captain America (2017) #695–704 — Waid/Samnee, "Home of the Brave" — OPTIONAL-STRONG. Restored Steve tours America rebuilding trust; deliberately small, and lovely.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block I6] Captain America (2018) #1–25
steps.text: [Era 05 Block I6] Captain America (2018) #1–25 — Ta-Nehisi Coates. Steve, publicly doubted after Hydra-Cap (the country saw him do it), rebuilds the idea of the shield against the Power Elite — with Sharon running her own war beside him. Sam's parallel tenure runs in his own appearances; the era file tiers this as the era's substantive Cap book.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.4] The 2022 dual books
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.4] The 2022 dual books — Captain America: Symbol of Truth #1–14 (Sam) + Sentinel of Liberty #1–11 (Steve) → Captain America: Finale #1 → Captain America (2023) #1–14 (Straczynski) — OPTIONAL as a whole, and the era file says why: the White Wolf / Outer Circle conspiracy is self-contained and feeds neither Blood Hunt nor One World Under Doom. Listed so its absence from the spine is a tiering decision.

steps.label: *[Era 06 §B9.1] ★ Captain America (2025) #1–11
steps.text: *[Era 06 §B9.1] ★ Captain America (2025) #1–11 — Zdarsky — MUST-READ for Armageddon. #1–5 "Our Secret Wars" (a retold early-days mission, deliberately mythic) → #6–11 "Doom's Shadow" (a reforming S.H.I.E.L.D., the Latverian crisis, a new Captain America figure — Dave Colton — and Red Hulk's move). Marvel and the guides treat it as Avengers: Armageddon*'s true first act; it is this track's current endpoint.

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Iron Man (1998) #73–78
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Iron Man (1998) #73–78 — EXPERT DEPTH selections. Tony becomes Secretary of Defense — the government role he carries into Disassembled and Civil War. (Skip Grell's earlier run except as the citation directs.)

steps.label: [Era 02 §5A] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 02 §5A] EVENT DIP — Disassembled's Iron Man front (Iron Man #84–89, inside Era 02 §5A's order). A drunk, compromised Tony is publicly destroyed — the run-up to his reinvention.

steps.label: *[Era 02 §5B.5] ★ Iron Man (2005) #1–6
steps.text: *[Era 02 §5B.5] ★ Iron Man (2005) #1–6 — EXTREMIS (Ellis).* The reboot: a designer virus rewrites Tony's body and the armour becomes part of him. Every modern Iron Man — comics and films — starts here.

steps.label: [Era 03 §2.3] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 03 §2.3] EVENT DIP — CIVIL WAR core. Tony leads the pro-registration side, builds the Thor clone and the Negative Zone prison, and wins — at the cost of Cap's surrender and death. Read inside the 24-step core (Track 4, step 6).

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.2] Iron Man: Director of S.H.I.E.L.D.
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.2] Iron Man: Director of S.H.I.E.L.D. — Tony takes over the world's security apparatus in the war's aftermath; the Mandarin's Extremis endgame is the run's keeper arc.

steps.label: [Era 03 §4.2] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 03 §4.2] EVENT DIP — SECRET INVASION. Tony's failure is total: his tech is compromised, his best friend's replacement is exposed, and Osborn takes his job in the peace. The invasion is the end of Tony's first empire.

steps.label: [Era 03 §5–§6] DARK REIGN
steps.text: [Era 03 §5–§6] DARK REIGN — Tony on the run. Inside Invincible Iron Man (2008): hunted by Osborn for the registration database, Tony deletes his own brain, backup by backup, to keep it out of reach — the Fraction run's first movement (#1–19; the era file takes Fraction's #1–33 as core-complete).

steps.label: *[Era 03 §6.2] ★ Invincible Iron Man #20–24
steps.text: *[Era 03 §6.2] ★ Invincible Iron Man #20–24 — "Stark: Disassembled" — MUST-READ. Tony, brain-deleted to near-vegetative, is rebooted from a backup made before Civil War* — the returned Tony has no memory of Civil War, Secret Invasion, or his own worst choices, and must be told what he did by the people he hurt. → "Stark Resilient" follows (the rebuild: a clean-energy company, a new armour, no absolution).

steps.label: [Era 03 §7.9] Fraction's second half (2010–11): the Resilient era concludes
steps.text: [Era 03 §7.9] Fraction's second half (2010–11): the Resilient era concludes — Detroit Steel, the Hammer girls, Tony's sobriety held under siege conditions.

steps.label: [Era 04 §2.2] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 04 §2.2] EVENT DIP — the Hickman spine's Tony. The Illuminati's most unrepentant member: he builds the planet-killers, survives Infinity (where he is also a Guardians guest — Track 5, step 11), and in Time Runs Out — inverted by AXIS (step 11) — is at his absolute worst when the worlds end.

steps.label: [Era 04 §5.5] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 04 §5.5] EVENT DIP — AXIS consequences (the event itself is SKIP; the consequences are this step). Tony stays inverted: Superior Iron Man (2014) #1–9 (Taylor) — OPTIONAL, "a sharp, nasty little run about Tony as a tech-bro villain" that explains his Time Runs Out behaviour. Know the fact even if you skip the book.

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.5] Iron Man (2012) #1–28
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.5] Iron Man (2012) #1–28 — Gillen — OPTIONAL; best arc #1–5 "Believe." Notable skip, named: "The Secret Origin of Tony Stark" (#9–17) — the adoption/Arno retcon consumed enormous attention in-era; later eras handle it in ways that make the original a poor time investment (Era 04 §10). Know the fact; skip the arc.

steps.label: [Era 04 §5.4] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL but consequential). Original Sin: Hulk vs. Iron Man #3.1–3.4
steps.text: [Era 04 §5.4] EVENT DIP (OPTIONAL but consequential). Original Sin: Hulk vs. Iron Man #3.1–3.4 — the same step as Track 8, step 9, from the other side: Tony's secret role in the gamma bomb. It feeds his Era 04 isolation.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block A1] Invincible Iron Man (2015) #1–5
steps.text: [Era 05 Block A1] Invincible Iron Man (2015) #1–5 — "Reboot" (Bendis). Post-Secret Wars Tony: a new armour, a new love (Amara), a missing-parents thread — and the debut-era of Riri Williams, who takes the book over during his Civil War II coma (the Invincible Iron Man (2016) run is her launch; read at the era file's tiering inside Blocks A/D).

steps.label: [Era 05 Block D] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 05 Block D] EVENT DIP — CIVIL WAR II minimal core. Tony leads the anti-prediction side against Carol — and ends the event in a coma, functionally dead. Minimal context is all the track needs; the era file's verdict on the event is "minimal/skip-with-explanation" and this track follows it.

steps.label: *[Era 05 Block C5] ★ Infamous Iron Man (2016) #1–12
steps.text: *[Era 05 Block C5] ★ Infamous Iron Man (2016) #1–12 — COMPLETE. The era's great Iron Man book is not Tony's: Victor von Doom, face healed by Secret Wars, takes up the armour to atone — and is terrifyingly good at being a hero. Read it as this track's centrepiece for 2016–17 (and as Track-adjacent Doom scholarship for One World Under Doom*).

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H8] The Search for Tony Stark
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H8] The Search for Tony Stark — SUMMARY ONLY (Invincible Iron Man #593–600). What you need: Tony wakes from the coma in a new body; Doom abandons the armour, ending step 16's arc. The era file tiers the hunt itself OPTIONAL.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block I9] Tony Stark: Iron Man (2018) #1–19
steps.text: [Era 05 Block I9] Tony Stark: Iron Man (2018) #1–19 — Slott — OPTIONAL (#1–5 sets the post-coma status quo: A.I. rights, Jocasta, Aaron Stack). Its real destination is Iron Man 2020, which lands at the next era's seam as a summary-level beat.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.4] Iron Man (2020) #1–25
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.4] Iron Man (2020) #1–25 — Cantwell — OPTIONAL (the Korvac saga; well-regarded, event-free). Then *Duggan's Invincible Iron Man (2022)*, filed by the era file inside the Fall of X treatment (Era 06 §A10.3) because it is a Fall of X book first — Tony loses everything to Feilong, an Orchis-adjacent industrialist, and marries Emma Frost as a business arrangement. Read it in that window.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B7–B8] EVENT DIPS
steps.text: [Era 06 §B7–B8] EVENT DIPS — BLOOD HUNT → ONE WORLD UNDER DOOM. Tony is an Avengers core member through both (Track 4, steps 28–29); Doom — his mirror since step 16 — ruling the world competently is the track's thematic endpoint.

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — 2000–2003 (honest). No Venom solo makes the main guide's cut, and the character's own early-2000s material is exactly the filler the guide exists to cut. Venom's first real step is as someone else's villain:

steps.label: [Era 02 §4.9] Marvel Knights Spider-Man (2004) #1–12
steps.text: [Era 02 §4.9] Marvel Knights Spider-Man (2004) #1–12 — the "Venomous" arc inside Millar's run (Track 1, step 3): Eddie Brock, dying, auctions the symbiote — it passes to Angelo Fortunato, then settles on Mac Gargan (the Scorpion). That transfer is the track's Era 03 status quo.

steps.label: [Era 03 §4.3] Amazing Spider-Man #568–573
steps.text: [Era 03 §4.3] Amazing Spider-Man #568–573 — "New Ways to Die." Anti-Venom debuts: Eddie Brock, cancer-free and symbiote-haunted, is transformed by Mr. Negative into a white inverse-Venom — while Gargan's Venom serves in Osborn's Thunderbolts across the street. The two-Venom status quo of the Dark Reign years in one arc.

steps.label: [Era 03 §5.1] CONTEXT DIP
steps.text: [Era 03 §5.1] CONTEXT DIP — Dark Avengers. Gargan-Venom wears a Spider-Man costume on Osborn's fake Avengers. No solo reading required; the era file's triad entry carries it — but know it, because step 5 is the redemption of exactly this idea.

steps.label: *[Era 03 §8.7] ★ Venom (2011) #1–5
steps.text: *[Era 03 §8.7] ★ Venom (2011) #1–5 — Remender — EXPERT DEPTH for this track (COMPLETIONIST for the spine). Agent Venom: Flash Thompson — Peter's old bully, a double-amputee Iraq veteran — bonded to the symbiote on a government leash, 48 hours at a time. The character's modern reinvention. Continues: the Spider-Island chapters, Venom* #6–8 (inside Era 03 §8.7's Spider-Island treatment).

steps.label: [Era 04 §4.4] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 04 §4.4] EVENT DIP — "Superior Venom" (Superior Spider-Man #22–26, inside Track 1 step 13). Flash confronts Otto-Spider-Man, who steals the symbiote and becomes something worse. The era's best Venom story is inside another character's book — the guide is blunt about that pattern for this whole era.

steps.label: [Era 04 §7.1] CONTEXT DIP
steps.text: [Era 04 §7.1] CONTEXT DIP — Venom joins the Guardians. Flash, in space, becomes the symbiote's ambassador — and the Guardians run's later arcs (Era 04 §7.1's skipped #14–27) contain the Klyntar reveal (the symbiotes' homeworld and true name). The era file skips those issues on a fast track; for this track, know the fact (symbiotes = Klyntar, a peacekeeping species Venom's line was corrupted from) — Cates's run (step 9) assumes it.
steps.note: Annotate-only (M39(c) option D): this step's substance - Flash Thompson's Klyntar reveal - sits in Guardians of the Galaxy (2013) #14-27, which the guide deliberately skips; the only §7.1-filed chunk, Guardians of the Galaxy (2013) #0.1, does not contain the described material, so no expansion is forced. The step text carries the fact the track needs.

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — 2015–2017 (honest). The Space Knight era and the Lee Price Venom (2016) relaunch are not in the main guide's cut; Eddie Brock reclaims the symbiote in that window (know the fact: by 2018, Eddie is Venom again, and Flash Thompson is dead — killed in Amazing Spider-Man #800's "Go Down Swinging" fallout, Track 1 step 15, which this track's readers should read as the handover).

steps.label: *[Era 05 Block I3] ★ Venom (2018) #1–16
steps.text: *[Era 05 Block I3] ★ Venom (2018) #1–16 — Donny Cates launches the Knull saga. A god is coming: Knull, creator of the symbiotes, imprisoned in a cage of them, waking up. Eddie meets Rex Strickland, learns the symbiotes' secret history (Vietnam, S.H.I.E.L.D.'s own sym-soldiers), and discovers he has a son — Dylan Brock*. The mythology every later step runs on.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block K] ★ EVENT
steps.text: [Era 05 Block K] ★ EVENT — ABSOLUTE CARNAGE (2019), core order at Block K1. Cates's payoff #1: Carnage, resurrected and Knull-touched, hunts every host who ever wore a symbiote for the codex in their spines. Eddie and Dylan's father-son core is the event's heart. (All other tie-ins OPTIONAL-to-SKIP; the Miles tie-in is the best of them — Track 2, step 13.)

steps.label: [Era 06 §B2.1–B2.2] The build-up completes: Cates's Venom through #25 (recap at §B2.1) → Venom (2018) #26–30
steps.text: [Era 06 §B2.1–B2.2] The build-up completes: Cates's Venom through #25 (recap at §B2.1) → Venom (2018) #26–30 — "Venom Beyond" — MUST. Dylan's powers emerge; Virus and the Maker's shadow (the Ultimate universe's corpse is not done with this track) set the event's stakes.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B2.3] ★ EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B2.3] ★ EVENT — KING IN BLACK (Dec 2020–Apr 2021), core order at the citation. Knull arrives and wins in the first issue — Earth is caged in symbiote, its heroes absorbed. Eddie dies winning. Dylan inherits; Eddie ascends — he becomes the new King in Black, the god of the symbiotes, omnipresent across his own hive. The track's axis flips here: from here on, Eddie is a cosmic entity and Dylan is the Earth-side Venom.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B2.4] Venom (2021)
steps.text: [Era 06 §B2.4] Venom (2021) — the Ewing/Ram V era, in the era file's split chunks: #1–10 (MUST #1–5 — two timelines: Dylan bonded and hunted on Earth; Eddie at the end of time learning he will become his own villain, Bedlam) → #11–23 STRONGLY (the Meridius reveal; Dark Web chapters #14–16 read in Era 06 §A8.3's order) → #24–33 OPTIONAL-to-RECOMMENDED (#24–27 the keepers). Deep-cut partner: Carnage (2022) #1–16 (OPTIONAL — Carnage god-hunting across the Nine Realms; only its endpoint matters to step 14).

steps.label: [Era 06 §B2.4] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B2.4] EVENT — VENOM WAR (2024) #1–5 — STRONGLY, core only. Eddie vs. Dylan, father vs. son, for the throne, while Meridius (a colder future Eddie) manipulates both. Outcome: the status quo shatters — Eddie ends up bonded to Carnage; Dylan keeps Venom, weakened.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B2.4] All-New Venom (2024) #1–10
steps.text: [Era 06 §B2.4] All-New Venom (2024) #1–10 — Ewing — OPTIONAL (delightful). A mystery-host Venom in a street-level, almost Silver-Age book. The host's identity is spoiler-guarded in the guide on purpose — it is revealed in step 16, and the reveal belongs to that entry. Numbering note (resolver-critical, per the era file): after #10 the series continues as Venom (2025) from legacy #250.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B6.3] EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B6.3] EVENT — DEATH SPIRAL (Feb–May 2026), nine-part Spider-Man/Venom crossover (order at the citation: alpha one-shot → Amazing Spider-Man (2025) #23–27 interleaved with Venom #255–257 + the Eddie Brock: Carnage chapters). A killer called Torment hunts the Spider/Venom circle; Paul Rabin is killed; and the crossover publicly lands step 15's guarded reveal — Mary Jane Watson is the All-New Venom host. Shared with Track 1, step 21.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B2.5] ★ EVENT
steps.text: [Era 06 §B2.5] ★ EVENT — QUEEN IN BLACK (Jul–Sep 2026) — the saga's capstone. Build-up first: Knull #1–5 (Knull returns; Hela takes his power) + Venom #250–254, #259. Core order at the citation: Queen in Black #1 → Hela one-shot → #2 → Venom #260 → Thor one-shot → #3 → #4 → #5 → Venom #262 (the finale from MJ's perspective). Hela, Queen in Black, commands the dead god's legions; Knull returns to reclaim his throne; the collision ends with Venomworld — the development Ewing seeded from step 13 onward. The symbiote line's endpoint at guide cut-off.

steps.label: GAP
steps.text: GAP — 2000–2005 (honest). Strange has no solo book in the main guide's Era 02 cut. He is a guest (the Illuminati's mystic, a Disassembled consultant — Track 4, steps 2/5 carry those beats). The track's first real step is a standalone:

steps.citation: Era 03 Side Track D / Era 02 §8.10 window
steps.label: *[Era 03 Side Track D / Era 02 §8.10 window] ★ Doctor Strange: The Oath (2006) #1–5
steps.text: *[Era 03 Side Track D / Era 02 §8.10 window] ★ Doctor Strange: The Oath (2006) #1–5 — Vaughan/Martin — EXPERT DEPTH-plus, standalone-in-616. Strange must solve his own* attempted murder while Wong is dying of cancer. The best Doctor Strange story of its decade and every later Strange writer's touchstone. (Fenced as a standalone gem by Era 03 §10; its 2006 window is Era 02 §8.10 — read it in either lane's window.)

steps.label: [Era 03 §3.1] CONTEXT DIP
steps.text: [Era 03 §3.1] CONTEXT DIP — New Avengers "Revolution" + the Dark Reign magic thread. Strange, exiled with the illegal Avengers, is shot through with the cost of the Vishanti's wars; by Era 03 §5.02 (New Avengers #51–54) a depowered, hunted Strange must name a successor — Brother Voodoo takes the mantle (an Era 04 seed the spine plants here).

steps.label: *[Era 03 §7.6] CONTEXT DIP
steps.text: *[Era 03 §7.6] CONTEXT DIP — New Avengers (2010) #1–6.* The magic-war arc: the Vishanti abandon Earth. That sentence is magic's status quo entering Era 04 — everything Aaron later breaks starts broken here.

steps.label: [Era 04 §2.2] THE SPINE'S STRANGE. Inside Hickman's interleave, Strange's arc is the saga's darkest solo threa
steps.text: [Era 04 §2.2] THE SPINE'S STRANGE. Inside Hickman's interleave, Strange's arc is the saga's darkest solo thread: he sells his soul for power (the blood Bible, Phase C), does the Illuminati's unforgivable work in the Great Society endgame, and by Secret Wars is Doom's sheriff and right hand on Battleworld (Era 04 §3.1 — he hid the life raft's survivors for years, and Doom kills him for the mercy of it). No solo book — the spine is his book this era. (New Avengers Annual #1, a Strange solo inside the spine, is the one OPTIONAL issue — Era 04 §2.2 flags it.)

steps.label: *[Era 05 Block A5] ★ Doctor Strange (2015) #1–10
steps.text: *[Era 05 Block A5] ★ Doctor Strange (2015) #1–10 — Jason Aaron — + Last Days of Magic one-shot (after #6). The Empirikul — science-crusaders who murder magic dimension by dimension — have already won everywhere else; Earth's magic is damaged goods and Strange pays for every spell in blood and worse. The era file's framing: magic itself came back from Secret Wars* wrong, and this run is where that's proven.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block C4] Doctor Strange (2015) #11–20
steps.text: [Era 05 Block C4] Doctor Strange (2015) #11–20 — Aaron's conclusion: the Last Days of Magic war ends with magic restored — diminished, rationed, and Strange diminished with it.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block H5] Doctor Strange #381–390
steps.text: [Era 05 Block H5] Doctor Strange #381–390 — Donny Cates (legacy numbering): Strange, stripped of the Sorcerer Supreme title (it sits with Loki, briefly and hilariously), steals power back from Las Vegas — which detonates directly into DAMNATION (2018) #1–4 (core at the citation): Mephisto's Hotel Inferno, Vegas raised as hell on Earth, and a midnight team of the magic-adjacent (Wong, Blade, Ghost Rider, Iron Fist) cleaning up Stephen's mess. Secret Empire's Vegas destruction (Track 4, step 22) is the prerequisite nobody states — the era file states it.

steps.label: [Era 05 Block I9] Doctor Strange (2018) #1–17
steps.text: [Era 05 Block I9] Doctor Strange (2018) #1–17 — Mark Waid — OPTIONAL. Strange loses magic (again) and goes to space to relearn it. Fun, inessential — the era file's words, kept.

steps.label: [Era 06 §B4.4] ★ THE MacKAY SEQUENCE
steps.text: [Era 06 §B4.4] ★ THE MacKAY SEQUENCE — read as one sequence, MUST: (1) The Death of Doctor Strange (2021) #1–5 — Stephen is murdered; a time-displaced younger Strange-backup and *Clea — now Sorcerer Supreme of Earth and the Dark Dimension — inherit the war. (2) Strange (2022) #1–10 — Clea holds the mantle and resurrects Stephen by inches against the Blasphemy Cartel. (3) Doctor Strange (2023) #1–18 — Stephen + Clea, married co-Supremes; the War of the Vishanti / General Strange saga (#6–18) is the sequence's masterpiece — and ends inside* the next step. (Rotation note: in the main order these chunks interleave with MacKay's Moon Knight — Track 6 — per Era 06 §B4's Cluster R4.)

steps.label: [Era 06 §B7] EVENT DIP
steps.text: [Era 06 §B7] EVENT DIP — BLOOD HUNT (2024) finale. Stephen loses the mantle — to Doom, who takes the Sorcerer Supreme title as his price for saving the world from the vampires. The era file's framing is the track's thesis: Blood Hunt is a theft from Stephen personally, which is why Doom's reign (step 12) is written as Strange's dark mirror.

steps.label: *[Era 06 §B8] EVENT DIP
steps.text: *[Era 06 §B8] EVENT DIP — ONE WORLD UNDER DOOM (2025) + Doctor Strange of Asgard. Doom rules Earth as Sorcerer Supreme; Stephen, exiled to Asgard's mystic margins (the Doctor Strange of Asgard* thread the era file files inside §B8), works the problem from outside the world Doom owns. Clea does not simply take the mantle back — the era file explains why, and the explanation is the MacKay sequence's whole argument (step 10).
